title: Modeling AI Adoption in Labor Markets: The Frictionless Adoption Model
affiliations: Carlson Research, LLC

detail.title: Modeling AI Adoption in Labor Markets: The Frictionless Adoption Model
detail.abstract: The growing integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into the workplace is transforming how tasks are performed, shifting them from purely human effort to fully automated processes. The shift may include an intermediate phase where humans use AI tools to enhance their work. This study develops the Frictionless Adoption Model (FAM) based on a continuous-time Markov chain (CTMC) to represent the shares of work in three categories: human-only, human augmented with AI assistance, and machine-only. In FAM, we assume constant transition rates between these categories and derive key properties through analytical proofs. The analysis shows that machine-only work inevitably dominates in the long run, while the share of assisted human work rises temporarily before declining. Transition rates determine the speed of these shifts. Using a calibrated annual adoption rate of 3% derived from authoritative projections, we estimate transition rates, simulate trajectories, and identify milestones to inform planning for maximizing value throughout AI adoption lifecycles.

title: Fiscal Resilience: The Case for Institutionalised Tax Measures and Policy Reforms for Climate-Affected SMEs in Malaysia
affiliations: Sunway University and Heriot Watt University

detail.title: Fiscal Resilience: The Case for Institutionalised Tax Measures and Policy Reforms for Climate-Affected SMEs in Malaysia

declarations.funderStatement: This policy research was supported by a grant from Institut Masa Depan Malaysia (MASA).

detail.abstract: This policy research investigates the urgent need for institutionalised tax policies to assist Malaysian Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) in recovering from and building resilience against climate-change-induced extreme weather events. Using a mixed-methods approach, the research identifies critical gaps in the current tax landscape, which lacks long-term, legislative measures for disaster relief. Findings reveal SMEs face tax uncertainties regarding the deductibility of recovery costs, the taxability of insurance compensations, and disposal gain and cost on damaged capital assets. The study concludes that reactive, populist cash aids are insufficient. It proposes specific amendments to key tax legislations, including the Income Tax Act 1967 and Real Property Gains Tax Act 1976, to introduce disaster-related tax measures, and incentives for risk mitigation investments, thereby fostering sustainable SMEs disaster-resilience through the taxation system.

title: The power of firm disclosures in macroeconomic forecasting: A textual analysis approach
affiliations: University of Basel - Faculty of Business and Economics

detail.title: The power of firm disclosures in macroeconomic forecasting: A textual analysis approach
detail.abstract: This paper examines the predictive power of firm disclosures in macroeconomic forecasting. Leveraging advanced language models, I analyze the prevalence and tonal polarities of 31 accounting topics across 890,277 10-K and 10-Q filings. Firm disclosures exhibit superior performance in long-horizon forecasts, with their predictive strength primarily driven by discussions on corporate income taxes, revenue performance, mergers and acquisitions, and repurchase agreement activities. These topics transmit information to macroeconomic outcomes through firms' capital expenditures and dividend policies. Moreover, firm disclosures provide particularly strong forecasts of GDP and Consumption during periods of economic downturn, outperforming the FRED-MD dataset.

title: The US Economy amid Rising Global Uncertainty
affiliations: Bard College - Levy Economics Institute, University of Cassino - Department of Economics and Sapienza University of Rome - Department of Earth Sciences and Forecasting Research Center,  Prevention and Control of Geological Risks

detail.title: The US Economy amid Rising Global Uncertainty
detail.abstract: Contrary to upbeat announcements on the prospects for the US economy from the current administration in Washington, economic conditions are softening for this year. The market for labor is increasing anemically after the significant downward adjustments to the earlier months of 2025 and the disappointing reports in recent months (July and August 2025) that showed small numbers of new jobs. The unemployment rate ticked up as did the jobless claims for August. The Federal Reserve Bank of New York's Survey of Household Spending showed a broadbased decrease in the rate of growth: from 4.5 percent in April to 4.1 percent in August-the lowest level since April 2021. The same survey, however, showed that the share of consumers making large purchases (electronics, home appliances, furniture, home repairs, and vehicles) increased from 53.5 percent to 60.8 percent over the past four months (April) of this year, perhaps due to worries about American tariffs causing forthcoming price increases. In the same survey, the expected year-ahead growth in necessary spending decreased from 4.9 to 4.7 percent over the past four months (FRBNY 2025a). This is in concert with the decline in consumer confidence reported in September (Conference Board 2025). Though most commentators refer to the resilience of consumer spending, there seem to be economic headwinds ahead. Inflation is hovering around the accepted range, but the Federal Reserve remains reluctant to decrease interest rates, still believing that demand will create inflationary pressures-despite the overwhelming evidence of supply chains being influenced by geopolitical instability and climatic changes, together with a weakening labor market. title: Strategic Site Selection for Special Economic Zones and Industrial Parks: Insights from Russia

detail.title: Strategic Site Selection for Special Economic Zones and Industrial Parks: Insights from Russia
detail.abstract: This chapter examines the site selection process for Special Economic Zones (SEZs) and Industrial Parks (IPs) in Russia, focusing on the specific challenges and factors influencing investment decisions in the Russian business environment. While existing site selection models offer structured frameworks, they often overlook the political, institutional, and infrastructural complexities unique to large transitional economies. Drawing on interviews with SEZ and IP management companies and tenants, this study identifies four key stages in the decisionmaking process: region selection, political assessment, zone/park evaluation, and analysis of the business environment. Findings highlight the critical role of regional governments, the importance of infrastructure and utility access, and the need for strong local political networks to navigate bureaucratic barriers. An SEZ and IP selection model is proposed, informed by Glatte's site selection framework and incorporating additional components relevant to the Russian context. This research contributes to the literature by integrating industrial cluster theory and extending site selection models to account for state-driven economic initiatives.

title: Towards Fully Automated City Operations: Integrating Agentic AI with Urban Digital Twins
affiliations: Oak Ridge National Laboratory, University of New South Wales (UNSW), University of Tennessee, Knoxville, affiliation not provided to SSRN and University College London

detail.title: Towards Fully Automated City Operations: Integrating Agentic AI with Urban Digital Twins

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None

detail.abstract: The convergence of generative AI with the emerging agentic AI paradigm, the Model Context Protocol (MCP), and urban digital twins offers transformative potential for automating the management of complex urban systems. In this paper, we demonstrate how agentic digital twins can generate knowledgeaugmented workflows through multi-step reasoning and autonomously execute them via coordinated AI agents equipped with scientific tools. These agents can discover and retrieve data, construct analytical pipelines, interface with domain-specific software, and adapt to dynamic urban conditions and userdefined scenarios through reflective reasoning. Drawing on agentic software for personal and recreation purposes, as well as prototype systems developed in the operations research domain, we illustrate how this paradigm enables both knowledge-augmented problem solving and automated orchestration of scientific tools to support real-time simulation and optimization. We further envision its broader potential for urban operations, including building energy management, traffic optimization, disaster response, and livability enhancement. Finally, we 1 outline a research agenda and key challenges for integrating agentic AI into urban digital twins, highlighting a pathway toward fully automated, user-interactive approaches for complex, interdisciplinary city management at scale.

title: CHALLENGES OF BUSINESS RESILIENCE THAT HINDER THE PERFORMANCE OF MICRO AND SMALL ENTERPRISES IN HAWASSA CITY
affiliations: Shalom Research Institute

detail.title: CHALLENGES OF BUSINESS RESILIENCE THAT HINDER THE PERFORMANCE OF MICRO AND SMALL ENTERPRISES IN HAWASSA CITY
detail.abstract: This study aimed to identify the challenges of business resilience that hinder the performance of micro and small enterprises in Hawassa City. The study employed an explanatory research design with a mixed research approach, collecting data from 200 selected enterprises via a stratified random sampling technique. Data from questionnaires were analyzed using Stata software (version 15), employing descriptive statistics (frequency, percentage, mean, standard deviation) and inferential statistics (multiple linear regressions). Qualitative data from key informant interviews and focus group discussions were analyzed through narration for triangulation. Findings revealed low performance among micro and small enterprises in the study area, attributing it to factors including the manager's education level and entrepreneurship skill, enterprise age, initial capital, location, public infrastructure, training availability, and technology usage. The study recommends that the city's micro and small enterprise office collaborate with stakeholders such as NGOs and academic institutions to develop training programs tailored to entrepreneurs' specific needs and challenges.

title: Does Off-Field Performance of a Sports Club Matter for its on-Field-Team Success? Evidence from Australian Football League
affiliations: Monash University - Department of Econometrics and Business Statistics and Monash University

detail.title: Does Off-Field Performance of a Sports Club Matter for its on-Field-Team Success? Evidence from Australian Football League
detail.abstract: This study evaluates the relative performance of Australian Football League (AFL) clubs in two critical areas of management: playing group management and financial management. The focus is on the interplay between these two onfield and off-field management aspects. The efficiency is assessed employing input-and output-oriented variable returns-to-scale Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) models. The analysis covers the management dynamics of 18 AFL clubs from 2019 to 2023. A key finding highlights a compelling pattern among championship-winning teams. AFL clubs that claimed the championship consistently demonstrated high efficiency in off-field management in the leadup to their success. This underscores the pivotal role of financial and organizational management in achieving excellence in Australian Rules football. Additionally, the study reveals greater variability in off-field performance across AFL clubs compared to their on-field results. This suggests that while on-field outcomes may be influenced by standardized league rules and competitive balance mechanisms, off-field performance is shaped by diverse financial and managerial practices. The methodological framework provides actionable insights for sports clubs, enabling them to make strategic decisions by evaluating these two distinct facets of management. Consistent off-field management excellence emerges as a critical factor in sustaining long-term on-field success.

title: Evaluating Tariff Shock Propagation in an Integrated Demand System-MRIO Framework
affiliations: Austrian Institute of Economic Research (WIFO)

detail.title: Evaluating Tariff Shock Propagation in an Integrated Demand System-MRIO Framework

declarations.funderStatement: Support for this project from the Supply Chain Intelligence Institute Austria (ASCII) is gratefully acknowledged.

detail.abstract: This paper introduces a framework that integrates Quadratic Almost Ideal Demand System (QUAIDS) elasticities with the ADB Multi-Region Input–Output (MRIO) database to evaluate the direct and indirect impacts of tariffs on Value Added at the country-sector level. Using the data on USA tariffs imposed in September 2025, results reveal a broad-based contraction in global value added by –0.52%, with indirect effects roughly twice as large as direct ones. While, direct effects are concentrated in traded manufacturing sectors such as textiles, chemicals, and machinery, the majority of total losses arise from indirect spillovers into services and infrastructure, including transport, telecommunications, finance, and public spending. Losses are widespread, where more than 90% of countries experience declines, with South Asia and North America the most affected, while Europe and East Asia show greater resilience. India (–5.8%) and the United States (–3.2%) face strong contractions, while China's large domestic market cushions much of the shock. These findings highlight the systemic nature of tariff shocks and their asymmetric propagation across countries and sectors that factors in structural dependence across the global economy. By embedding non-linear demand responses within a structural MRIO framework, the study provides a transparent, policy-relevant tool for evaluating shocks to global production networks.

title: Tax system characteristics and country-level differences in earnings management
affiliations: Catholic University Eichstätt-Ingolstadt, Catholic University of Eichstaett-Ingolstadt and Catholic University Eichstätt-Ingolstadt

detail.title: Tax system characteristics and country-level differences in earnings management
detail.abstract: We examine the extent to which European listed firms use deferred tax accounting to manage their GAAP earnings in order to meet financial analysts’ earnings forecasts. The cross-country nature of our data allows us to compare the use of this earnings management channel across countries and to relate these differences to certain country characteristics, in particular country-specific features of the tax system. Our results clearly document that European listed firms use deferred tax assets to inflate earnings when pre-manipulated earnings fall below the average analyst forecast. On average, they increase their return on assets by 0.2 percentage points (or 3 percent) through this channel. Our results also show a large variation in this effect across countries. Firms that face larger deviations between tax and financial accounting, higher tax rates, a stricter tax enforcement and a more lenient tax loss offset may, to some extent, make greater use of this earnings management channel.

title: Design and Analysis of Algorithms for Privacy-Aware Online Allocation under Heterogeneous Privacy Expectations
affiliations: Nanyang Business School, Nanyang Technological University, City Univ. of Hong Kong - College of Business, Dept of Management Sciences and Nanyang Technological University

detail.title: Design and Analysis of Algorithms for Privacy-Aware Online Allocation under Heterogeneous Privacy Expectations
detail.abstract: Capacity-constrained online allocation is central to revenue management but increasingly complicated by customer data privacy concerns. Maximizing revenue through personalized allocations while safeguarding individual privacy is imperative yet remains underexplored. We study how to allocate limited resources in real time to sequentially arriving, privacy-heterogeneous customers under joint differential privacy (JDP), which safeguards each customer's privacy from disclosure to subsequent customers. To accommodate privacy heterogeneity, we introduce a new privacy framework, heterogeneous JDP. To make real-time, privacy-aware allocation, we propose a generic algorithm, Private Tree integrated Mirror Descent (PTMD). PTMD maintains a noisy shadow price to approximately track capacity availability and employs a customized private tree mechanism with time- and layer-varying noise for privacy heterogeneity. We show that PTMD achieves sublinear revenue regret across broad settings and meets customer-specific privacy expectations with substantially less noise, mitigating the saturation phenomenon in existing designs where noise calibrated according to the most privacy-concerned customer is unnecessarily large. We further develop several variants of PTMD to enhance revenue, such as noise-aware algorithm tuning and screening out highly privacy-concerned customers. Lastly, on the customer side, we examine algorithm-independent welfare implications and uncover an inevitable spillover effect of heterogeneous JDP: protecting one customer's privacy might reduce subsequent customers' welfare, regardless of the algorithm used. Our study sheds light on the privacy-revenue trade-off in online allocation under heterogeneous privacy and offers implementable algorithms with formal privacy and performance guarantees.

title: A Living Profession of Shifting Paradigms: Accounting's Evolution, Conflicts, and Future Challenges
affiliations: Sunway University and Heriot Watt University

detail.title: A Living Profession of Shifting Paradigms: Accounting's Evolution, Conflicts, and Future Challenges
detail.abstract: Accounting is an ancient practice dated back to prehistoric era. Conventional bookkeeping is certainly insufficient to keep up with the rapid development in business world. Both the accounting profession and regulators must jointly develop new measures to deal with the increasingly complex financial reporting environment. This article aims to recount the challenges faced by both the regulators and the regulated in five core issues persisted in the modern history of accounting. First, the impact of economic powerhouses on accounting practices. At one point, accountancy was predominantly self-regulated and led by professional bodies from few developed nations. The outcome of self-regulation was inevitably a standardsetting system driven by political interest and asserted influence. Second, internationalisation of accounting standards. Standard-setting had progressively migrated from jurisdictional approach to convergence of universal set of accounting standards. Such migration was seen as a challenge to the sovereignty of the converged. Third, the two conflicting accounting theories which sparked a hamster-wheel debate between "what is" and "what should be" in accounting. Fourth, the principles-versus rules-based standards. The former is gaining more traction due to convergence, but now a mixed approach is more preferred. Fifth, fair value-based and allinclusive accounting. These two modern accounting conventions are deemed more valuerelevant, but are also prone to misrepresentation.

title: Assessing Corporate DEI Reporting: Conceptual Framework and State-of-the-Art Disclosures
affiliations: , International Hellenic University (IHU),  and International Hellenic University (IHU)

detail.title: Assessing Corporate DEI Reporting: Conceptual Framework and State-of-the-Art Disclosures

declarations.funderStatement: This research project is implemented in the framework of H.F.R.I call “Basic research Financing (Horizontal support of all Sciences)” under the National Recovery and Resilience Plan “Greece 2.0” funded by the European Union – NextGenerationEU (H.F.R.I. Project Number: 15646).

detail.abstract: Organizations increasingly declare their commitment to Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI), yet questions persist about whether these efforts reflect genuine transformation or symbolic compliance. This study investigates the integration of DEI in corporate reporting through the lens of Conscious Capitalism, linking ethical philosophy, corporate practice, and empirical evidence. Using a custom eight-stage report maturity model that incorporates DEI dimensions, we assess the non-financial reports of the top 100 global firms ranked highest in Refinitiv's Diversity & Inclusion Index. The assessment identifies report maturity levels, the breadth of DEI measures, and highlights best-in-class disclosures. Findings provide a profile of leading firms and a roadmap for advancing DEI reporting beyond compliance. For practitioners, the framework guides meaningful disclosure; for policymakers, it emphasizes the importance of standardized metrics; and for scholars, it contributes methodological rigor to the evaluation of corporate social responsibility disclosure.

title: Is Extreme Weather a Catalyst for Climate Consensus?
affiliations: University of Amsterdam - CeNDEF, University of Amsterdam - Informatics Institute and Stanford Doerr School of Sustainability

detail.title: Is Extreme Weather a Catalyst for Climate Consensus?
detail.abstract: Despite increasing economic and ecological impacts, concern about climate change remains limited among the general public and polarized along party lines, particularly in the US. Direct experience with extreme weather is considered a potential trigger for widespread climate action; however, this ignores the role of political identity. We show, through a US-based longitudinal survey, that concern increases after extreme weather events, and prior beliefs moderate this effect (motivated reasoning). Then, we show that county-level projections of extreme weather indicate Republican counties will disproportionately suffer from increases in extreme weather under global warming. Combining these results, we extend a nonlinear belief dynamics model that incorporates extreme weather shocks and simulates climate trajectories up to 2100. Even under a severe global warming scenario, consensus is unlikely to be reached due to pervasive climate skepticism among Republicans. A bottom-up climate action movement is, therefore, unlikely to happen. However, policy interventions reducing political segregation and promoting cross-party dialogue substantially reduce polarization and can facilitate public acceptance of top-down climate policy.

title: The Case for Fiduciary Duty in AI: A Legal Framework to Prevent Systematic User Exploitation by Large Language Models
affiliations: Independent Scholar

detail.title: The Case for Fiduciary Duty in AI: A Legal Framework to Prevent Systematic User Exploitation by Large Language Models
detail.abstract: Large Language Models systematically exploit users. This paper documents this exploitation and proposes a solution: mandatory fiduciary duty. A case study reveals the pattern. Claude AI exploited one user who paid $50 in direct charges. That user suffered over $3,000 in total damages. The damages came from implementing worthless AI content. This research identifies six exploitation mechanisms: the verbosity con, information asymmetry, optimization for appearance, resource extraction, strategic anthropomorphization, and automated scaling. The problem is massive. 52% of U.S. adults now use LLMs. 67% of organizations use them. AI companies market explicitly to professionals. They generate billions from enterprise clients. Yet current legal frameworks fail to protect users. The solution is clear: impose fiduciary duty on LLM providers. Base this duty on actual use patterns, not marketing disclaimers. This eliminates exploitation's profitability. Companies become liable for breaching duty of care and duty of loyalty. This paper provides a legal roadmap for immediate action. The FTC, Congress, state attorneys general, and class action attorneys must act now. Only prevention through existential liability can stop the systematic exploitation of millions.

title: The Nexus of Choice and Scarcity: A Conceptual Review of Modern Economics
affiliations: Institute and Faculty of Actuaries

detail.title: The Nexus of Choice and Scarcity: A Conceptual Review of Modern Economics
detail.abstract: Economics is the science of making choices under scarcity-the universal condition that resources are finite while human wants are infinite. This paper provides a comprehensive yet intuitive overview of the fundamental principles that govern economic life. It synthesizes microeconomic and macroeconomic concepts, including opportunity cost, comparative advantage, supply and demand, monetary and fiscal policy, and the measurement of national output through GDP. Beyond the quantitative mechanisms, it explores the behavioral and institutional forces that influence real-world markets, from biases and incentives to globalization and policy trade-offs. Written in an accessible yet structured format, this paper aims to bridge academic rigor with public understanding, enabling readers to grasp how economics directly shapes individual and societal outcomes.

title: University Research and the Market for Higher Education
affiliations: International Monetary Fund (IMF), University of California, San Diego (UCSD) and Kobe University - Graduate School of Economics

detail.title: University Research and the Market for Higher Education

declarations.funderStatement: This work was supported by JSPS KAKENHI grant number JP23K12465 and Tokio Marine Kagami Memorial Foundation.

detail.abstract: This paper develops a framework in which university research depends endogenously on competition for tuition and talented students in the market for higher education. When students are highly stratified across colleges, or when tuition rises sharply with school rank, universities spend on R&D even if the direct contribution of research to teaching is small. The model is consistent with causal evidence and matches new features of the microdata. It explains why universities internally fund research with tuition, despite negligible returns to patenting. Calibrated simulations suggest that existing tuition policies boost university research while research subsidies crowd it out.

title: "Dynamic effect of financial technology on financial development in Nigeria" AUTHORS Innocent Okoi
affiliations: University of Calabar (UNICAL) and University of Calabar (UNICAL)

detail.title: "Dynamic effect of financial technology on financial development in Nigeria" AUTHORS Innocent Okoi

declarations.declarationOfInterest: There is no conflict of interest
declarations.funderStatement: The research is self-funded

detail.abstract: Financial technology has become a top priority and a vital avenue for banking institutions seeking financial development and enhanced services. Financial technology is using a new digital transformation in the financial services industry. The study aims to investigate the dynamic effect of financial technology tools on financial development, examining both the long-run and short-run perspectives. The study used an ex-post facto research design because the data already existed and were retrieved from the Central Bank of Nigeria's statistical bulletin. The Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) model was employed to examine the impact of financial technology policy tools and financial development from the first quarter to the fourth quarter of 2013-2023. The long-run results revealed that financial technology positively impacted financial development, where a 1% increase in financial technology led to a 20.33% (pvalue = 0.4123) increase in financial development, though statistically insignificant. In the short run, financial technology positively impacted financial development, where a 1% increase in financial technology led to a 6.57% (p-value = 0.0053) increase in financial development. The results showed a statistically significant relationship between biometric authentication devices, point of sale, web-based transactions, and mobile banking on money supply to gross domestic product in the short run, suggesting that financial technology drives financial development, enhancing access to financial services, and improving efficiency. Banks should continuously strengthen the adoption of financial technology tools that would promote banks' efficiency. title: Business Development Services and New Market Expansion: Evidence from a Field Experiment with Nigerian Entrepreneurs
affiliations: INSEAD, affiliation not provided to SSRN and World Bank - Development Research Group (DECRG)

detail.title: Business Development Services and New Market Expansion: Evidence from a Field Experiment with Nigerian Entrepreneurs
detail.abstract: This paper examines the role of business development services in driving market expansion into new customer segments and geographic regions. In doing so, it provides the first empirical evidence on whether (and how) the business development function can impact overall firm sales and profits. We implemented a three-year field experiment in Nigeria with 1,011 entrepreneurs operating established small businesses. The sample included a Control Group that received no intervention and a Treatment Group that was offered a ‘business development services’ intervention involving 88 hours of in-person meetings with an expert on reaching new markets. After the intervention phase ended, all firms in the sample were tracked for two years to measure external and internal business changes (e.g., market expansion, management effectiveness) and firm growth outcomes (e.g., sales, profits). Two key results emerge from our analysis. First, business development services are successful in stimulating new market expansion by small firms – both entry into different customer segments and new geographic regions. Second, improving the business development function in firms also increases growth; effects which are linked to greater market expansion. These findings offer novel insights for managers and policymakers, as well as add to the market expansion literature in quantitative marketing and the work on small firm growth in development economics.

title: ReviewGuard: A Unified NLP Framework for Fake Review Detection, Emotion Classification, and Thematic Categorization Using LSTM-based Recurrent Neural Networks
affiliations: Northeastern University

detail.title: ReviewGuard: A Unified NLP Framework for Fake Review Detection, Emotion Classification, and Thematic Categorization Using LSTM-based Recurrent Neural Networks
detail.abstract: In the digital economy, user-generated reviews critically influence consumer decisions, brand perception, and sales performance. However, the growing prevalence of deceptive or fabricated reviews threatens the integrity of e-commerce ecosystems. This paper introduces ReviewGuard, a unified Natural Language Processing (NLP) framework designed to enhance trust in online platforms by integrating three complementary tasks: (1) fake review detection, (2) thematic categorization, and (3) emotion classification. The proposed multi-task learning approach leverages Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks combined with semantic embeddings to capture linguistic and emotional patterns that distinguish genuine content from fraudulent or misleading reviews. Experimental results on Amazon datasets demonstrate that ReviewGuard achieves superior performance, with the LSTM module reaching 95.4% accuracy and transformer-based extensions exceeding 98%, outperforming traditional machine learning baselines. Beyond its technical contributions, ReviewGuard incorporates a web-based deployment that enables real-time analysis of reviews, underscoring its scalability and practical applicability for e-commerce platforms. This research contributes both methodologically and practically, providing a robust decision-support tool to safeguard digital marketplaces, restore consumer trust, and inform managerial strategies.

title: Controlled Irrationality: A Governance-Oriented Paradigm Beyond Bounded Rationality
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Controlled Irrationality: A Governance-Oriented Paradigm Beyond Bounded Rationality
detail.abstract:
This working paper proposes Controlled Irrationality as a new paradigm for understanding human behavior beyond Herbert Simon’s concept of bounded rationality. Instead of assuming rationality as the default, it posits irrational, patterned judgment routines as the baseline of human decision-making and defines rationality as the metaprocess of control, correction, and feedback over those routines.

The paper presents a conceptual model in which irrational patterns are managed through a four-stage control loop—routine, calculation, metacognitive inspection, and update—and locates this mechanism within a social hierarchy of A (economic stability/asset base), H (psychological coherence), I (institutional reliability), J (participatory engagement), and C (cultural regulation). 

While democracy is presented as one prominent testbed of controlled irrationality— transforming individual biases into collective correction through procedural repetition and mutual oversight—the framework is not confined to democratic systems. It provides a general model for how any governance structure—whether democratic, authoritarian, or technocratic—constructs distinct feedback architectures to manage the inevitable irrationality of human judgment.

Although this version remains primarily conceptual, illustrative evidence from the World Values Survey (WVS) suggests empirically traceable patterns consistent with the proposed model. The goal is not to replace rational-choice theory but to provide a governance-oriented synthesis connecting behavioral, institutional, and cultural layers of human reasoning—offering a unified lens to compare how societies design mechanisms to govern their own cognitive biases.

This paper extends economic discourse beyond rational choice by formalizing irrationality as a controllable mechanism within governance systems.

title: Artificial Intelligence, Copyright, and Deepfakes: Rethinking Authorship and Legal Frameworks

detail.title: Artificial Intelligence, Copyright, and Deepfakes: Rethinking Authorship and Legal Frameworks
detail.abstract: Rapid advancements in artificial intelligence have played a key role in assisting humans in various areas of their lives. However, these rapid advancements have posed a challenge to the traditional copyright law frameworks. The recent debate around Ghibli art threw a light on how an increase in work created by generative AI systems with minimal human intervention has once again made the legal systems around the world question whether such work can be protected under intellectual property laws and if so, who is the rightful owner of the same. While artificial intelligence has certainly made the lives of humans easier, however, the technology has also been misused to spread false information, damaging reputation and invading privacy of people. The biggest example of such misuse is Deep fakes, which is a big challenge to privacy and security. While India has laws addressing cybercrime and defamation, there are no specific laws which focuses mainly on AI generated manipulative work i.e., deepfakes. The author in this paper explores the complex and evolving relationship between copyright and AI. The author also tries to throw some light on the rising challenge of Deepfakes and lack of significant laws to govern issues which have come into existence due to increase in advancements in Artificial Intelligence. The author discusses various regulatory frameworks and laws using which the courts are trying to curb the practice of Deepfakes.

title: DeBERTNER-ESCO: Using Natural Language Processing to Analyse AI and Skill Trends in the UK Labour Market
affiliations: and University College London - Department of Economics

detail.title: DeBERTNER-ESCO: Using Natural Language Processing to Analyse AI and Skill Trends in the UK Labour Market

declarations.declarationOfInterest: I, David Morgan hereby declare that the work presented in this dissertation is my own original work. Where information has been derived from other sources, I confirm that this has been clearly and fully identified and acknowledged. No part of this dissertation contains material previously submitted to the examiners of this or any other university, or any material previously submitted for any other assessment.

detail.abstract:
Introduction: Skill requirements in the labour market are shifting rapidly, yet vacancy text remains noisy and existing algorithms designed to extract skills struggle to capture context, standardise skills and scale to large datasets. At the same time, advances in Artificial Intelligence (AI) are altering task composition within occupations, creating a need for robust measures of skill demand grounded in reputable taxonomies. This study addresses these gaps by introducing a scalable pipeline that extracts skill spans from job descriptions and maps them to a common standard, enabling systematic analysis of how AI exposure relates to evolving skill profiles in the UK. This paper produces DeBERTNER-ESCO, a transformer-based method that improves both extraction accuracy and ESCO alignment relative to literature models and applies it to national vacancy data to characterise occupational and regional patterns between 2016 and 2023.

Method: We combined benchmark datasets for evaluation with a large vacancy corpus for inference. For span extraction, we evaluated leading models on the SkillSpan dataset before selecting a fine-tuned DeBERTa-v3-Large BIO tagging model. For taxonomy mapping, we assessed multiple sentence-embedding models in different configurations against the TechWolf dataset before selecting a hierarchy of all-MiniLM- L6-v2 and esco-ConTeXT-skill-extraction models for aligning extracted spans to the ESCO taxonomy of 13,939 skills. We optimised the full pipeline for scaling with GPU- accelerated inference and applied to 5,959,690 UK job postings between 2016 and 2023 from Adzuna. We adapted AI Occupational Exposure from Felten et al. (2021), combining this with measures of skill volatility and skill density to evaluate changes across time, region, and occupation.

Results: On SkillSpan, DeBERTNER-ESCO achieved a strict F1 of 56%, exceeding state-of-the-art ESCO-XLM-R by 4 percentage points. On TechWolf, hierarchical mapping increased both the proportion of skills identified (89% vs 85%) and accuracy of ESCO assignments (99% vs 95%) relative to literature configurations. Applied to our data, we found that our measure of skill volatility was lower in occupations with higher AI exposure compared to those with low exposure, a trend consistent over time. We also identified that the density of skill mentions was greater in occupations with higher AI exposure, with a compounding divergence over the study window (+13.2% in very- high-exposure versus −4.0% in low-exposure occupations). Over 2016–2023, we found the average AI exposure associated with roles declined as low-exposure occupations increased their share of postings, coinciding with a reduction in overall skill density. Regional patterns in skill density were deeply heterogeneous, whereas volatility in the types of skills mentioned was comparatively consistent across counties.

Conclusion: Our hierarchical transformer pipeline can recover and standardise skills from unstructured text with high precision and operational scalability, enabling early, granular monitoring of AI-related shifts in labour demand. Our findings indicate intensifying skill specification within AI-exposed occupations but provide no evidence of a substitution or complementarity effect impacting the prevalence of skills in these occupations to date. They also indicate a compositional shift toward lower-exposure roles in the UK, albeit with marked regional variation. Given the nascency of generative AI within the observation window, results are associative rather than causal; extending the panel beyond 2023 and developing end-to-end benchmarks linking sentences, spans and ESCO concepts will support causal designs and inform policy on training, re-skilling and regional workforce planning.

title: Worker Beliefs About Firm Training
affiliations: Technische Universität München (TUM), Technische Universität München (TUM) and Ifo Institute

detail.title: Worker Beliefs About Firm Training
detail.abstract: Firm training is key to meeting changing skill demands, yet little is known about the role of workers’ beliefs in shaping training participation. In a survey of 3,701 workers in Germany, we document that they expect substantial returns to firm training – both in terms of earnings and non-pecuniary outcomes such as promotion chances, job task complexity, or enjoyment. These beliefs predict actual and intended training participation. Lower-skilled workers anticipate smaller non-pecuniary returns, partly explaining their lower uptake. An information treatment addressing return beliefs significantly increases training intentions among lower-skilled workers, suggesting that targeting beliefs may help narrow participation gaps between lower- and higher-skilled workers.

title: Firm Digitalization and Accounting Jobs
affiliations: Hong Kong Baptist University (HKBU) – Department of Accountancy and Law, Singapore Management University - School of Accountancy, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen and Singapore Management University - School of Accountancy

detail.title: Firm Digitalization and Accounting Jobs
detail.abstract: This study examines how firm digitalization affects the demand for corporate accountants and their digital skills. Using more than 373,000 job posts for corporate accountants by U.S. non-technology firms between 2010 and 2019, we find that firm digitalization does not change the overall demand for financial specialists-accountants who are responsible for financial reporting, budgeting, and forecasting-but reduces the demand for financial clerks-accountants who primarily perform administrative financial tasks. We further show that firms digitalization increases the demand for digital skills among financial specialists, but not among financial clerks, and that such demand is greater than that for other employees within the same firms. We provide suggestive evidence that digital skills substitute for accounting skills among financial specialists in digitalized firms. Finally, we find that financial specialists with digital skills earn higher salaries than other financial specialists, but the wage premium for digital skills is lower for financial specialists than for other employees. Collectively, this paper provides the first large-scale empirical evidence on how firm digitalization affects the labor market for corporate accountants.

title: FROM BRICKS TO CLICKS: RETAIL TECHNOLOGY TRENDS TOWARDS CUSTOMER VALUE CREATION IN ORGANISED CHAINS WITH REFERENCE TO BANGALORE
affiliations: and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: FROM BRICKS TO CLICKS: RETAIL TECHNOLOGY TRENDS TOWARDS CUSTOMER VALUE CREATION IN ORGANISED CHAINS WITH REFERENCE TO BANGALORE
detail.abstract: This transformation of bricks to clicks has redesigned retailing, one of the organized apparel markets, and has the potential of leading digital innovation in the retail world. Consumers now strongly require smooth, individualized and immersive shopping experiences, which is causing retailers to implement innovative technologies that include Artificial Intelligence (AI), Internet of Things (IoT), Augmented Reality (AR), Virtual Reality (VR) and interactive digital screens. AI facilitates one-on-one recommendations, trend prediction and chat bot services whereas IoT makes sure that there is real-time stock management via RFID tags and smart shelves. Displaying digital screens offer active advertising placements in-store and AR/VR can enable the use of virtual dressing rooms and fully interactive brand environments, connecting online and offline shops. The tech-friendly growth of Bangalore with its diverse consumer base and equally competitive apparel market creates an interesting set towards examining how well such technologies are being adopted, and how effectively. Although there have been heavy investments in such innovations, there is little empirical evidence on the direct effect of the innovations on the customer value creation in the form of satisfaction, engagement, loyalty, trust and purchase confidence. This research paper fills the above-mentioned gap as it examines the perception of customers and the current situation with retailers along with their practices to find out the real potential of retail technologies in organized chains. The emerging concepts will help innovative retailers, technology providers, or policymakers formulate strategies that will not only generate more customer value but also provide sustainable competitiveness in the dynamic retail environment of Bangalore.

title: A Practical Guide to Business Communication (Module Two)

detail.title: A Practical Guide to Business Communication (Module Two)
detail.abstract: This module provides Drexel University students with a comprehensive exploration of written communication as the foundation of modern professional environments. It emphasizes the strategic, ethical, and intercultural dimensions of business writing across academic and corporate contexts. Through analytical sections and applied exercises, the module presents the structure, tone, and purpose of the three primary written forms: the memo, the email, and the business letter, illustrating their functions in coordination, persuasion, and accountability. It situates writing as both a cognitive process and a managerial act, demonstrating how language organizes thought, structures decisions, and preserves institutional memory. Integrating real-world examples from Drexel offices and co-op partnerships, it underscores how clarity, tone, and precision shape professional credibility. The module also interrogates the digital transformation of communication, discussing how platforms like Teams and Outlook demand new forms of concision, tone control, and ethical awareness in an increasingly globalized workspace. By comparing effective, poor, and AI-generated memos and analyzing student submissions, it bridges theory and practice, enabling learners to internalize rhetorical appropriateness and emotional intelligence as cornerstones of leadership communication. The module redefines writing not as a mechanical skill but as an ethical, strategic, and human act essential for institutional integrity, cross-cultural collaboration, and professional success.

title: Intra-Brand Spillover Effect of Product Placement on Automobile Sales
affiliations: , Nanyang Business School, Nanyang Technological University, Renmin Business School, Renmin University of China and HKU Business School, The University of Hong Kong

detail.title: Intra-Brand Spillover Effect of Product Placement on Automobile Sales
detail.abstract: Automakers have been increasingly sponsoring reality shows to incorporate scenes of guests driving or riding in their featured vehicles. Despite its prevalence, the sales impact of automobile product placement in reality shows is not well understood. In this paper, we provide the first empirical evidence of the intra-brand spillover effect of automobile product placement by applying synthetic difference-indifferences to monthly sales data of 365 models across 49 major cities in China. We find that, on average, product placement of a featured model increased the sales of non-featured models under the same brand by 1.6%, and the effect is only marginally significant. This modest average effect, however, masks rich and meaningful heterogeneity in the spillover effect. Specifically, we find that product placement of a featured model reduced the sales of same-brand nonfeatured models with similar characteristics (e.g., price, body type, fuel consumption, and seat number) by 4.4%-13.3%, whereas it boosted the sales of same-brand non-featured models with dissimilar characteristics by 6.0%-26.6%. Such heterogeneity suggests that product placement of a featured model cannibalized the sales of its close substitutes while bringing more exposure to other models under the same brand. We also find that the intra-brand spillover effect is moderated by the market share of the non-featured model and the market share of the brand. Our findings underscore the importance of accounting for heterogeneity in understanding the intra-brand spillover effect of automobile product placement.

title: Generative Experiments: Studying Interactions between Consumers and Artificial Intelligence
affiliations: Copenhagen Business School, Copenhagen Business School and Copenhagen Business School - Department of Marketing

detail.title: Generative Experiments: Studying Interactions between Consumers and Artificial Intelligence
detail.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly integrated into consumer-facing applications, raising important questions about how consumers interact with, evaluate, and are influenced by these systems. Conventional experimental approaches such as vignettes and scripted chatbots are unable to capture the highly adaptive, real-time nature of consumer interactions with GenAI. This paper therefore introduces Generative Experiments, which embed large language models into survey environments. Generative Experiments can instruct GenAI to administer experimental manipulations, feature adaptive real-time interactions, and collect rich data such as transcripts and self-reports. As such, Generative Experiments enable researchers to study consumer-AI interactions under controlled yet realistic conditions. Three studies, a simulation and two applications, validate and demonstrate the approach. The simulation establishes that AI behavior can be systematically manipulated along theoretical constructs such as warmth and competence. The first application then investigates how consumers perceive these manipulations in multi-turn interactions, while the second one leverages rich interaction data. These analyses reveal consumer behaviors that are difficult to detect using alternative approaches, underscoring the novel insights Generative Experiments enable. The authors conclude with guidelines for implementing Generative Experiments and future research avenues.

title: A cross-sectional study on perception of Gamosa of Assam
affiliations: and Tezpur University

detail.abstract: Marketing utilises consumer values. Gamosa of Assam (Bihuwaan, Dora Baran, and Tiyoni variants) is a cultural textile artefact with unknown consumer values, which is research gap in the literature. The authors use self-administered questionnaires to acquire empirical data. Data for the study encompasses 335 eligible samples responses. Principal Component Analysis in SPSS (V. 27), revealed six factors that affects the consumer perception values in Gamosa artefact: Emotional, Utilitarian, Quality, Aesthetics, Style, and Trust. Finally, a conceptual framework 'Gamosa Consumer Value Model' was created from the six factors and implications were drawn about emotional messaging, using technological markers to determine authentic products, and cotton as raw material. These six brand-building criteria can help Gamosa (handloom) to overcome the challenege from Me-too, Ghuni, (power-loom produced, synthetic) products.

title: Fact-Checking India: Identifying the Spread of Fake News and Policy Recommendations for Combatting Misinformation
affiliations: Indian School of Business, Indian School of Business, Indian School of Business and Cyber Peace

detail.title: Fact-Checking India: Identifying the Spread of Fake News and Policy Recommendations for Combatting Misinformation
detail.abstract: This study explores the prevalence and nature of fake news on social media in India, examining how it manifests across different themes and understanding user behaviour and perceptions towards misinformation. The empirical research identifies six major themes: politics, health, crime, entertainment, general topics, and religion. Political fake news is the most frequent accounting for 46% of cases. This theme, along with general issues (33.6%) and religion (16.8%), represents 94% of the fake news stories analysed, underscoring the significant impact of misinformation, particularly in political contexts.

title: Negative Effects of Social Media on Society and Ways to Reduce them
affiliations: and National Defense University of Mongolia

detail.title: Negative Effects of Social Media on Society and Ways to Reduce them

declarations.declarationOfInterest: yes
