title: If We Fail to Solve Global Climate Change, Blame the Nuclear Regulatory Commission
affiliations: Drake University - Law School

detail.title: If We Fail to Solve Global Climate Change, Blame the Nuclear Regulatory Commission

publicationDetails.detailsText: Case Western Reserve Law Review, Volume 75, Issue 1 pp. 177-231

detail.abstract: This Article argues that the chief obstacle to solving global climate change is not technology but regulation. Nuclear power, the only scalable carbon-free energy source, remains paralyzed by the institutional incentives of the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC). Drawing on public choice theory, law and economics, and administrative law, the Article shows how the NRC’s risk aversion, regulatory capture, and rent-seeking dynamics have transformed it from a promoter of innovation into a barrier to energy policy modernization. The 2019 Nuclear Energy Innovation and Modernization Act (NEIMA) sought reform but left the agency’s discretion intact. Combining political economy and institutional design analysis, the Article concludes that unless regulation changes, nuclear innovation will remain stifled and climate mitigation impossible. If humanity fails to decarbonize, the blame will lie not with markets or technology, but with the regulators who made perfection the enemy of progress.

title: Pax-Americana: US Military Power and the Global Dollar Cycle
affiliations: Northwestern University, Kellogg School of Management

detail.title: Pax-Americana: US Military Power and the Global Dollar Cycle
detail.abstract: This paper proposes a general equilibrium model in which U.S. military hegemony-the Pax Americana-acts as a non-rival global public good that stabilizes the world economy and anchors the dominance of the U.S. dollar. The U.S. security umbrella lowers geopolitical risk and contractenforcement frictions, allowing allies to reallocate resources from defense to welfare and public investment. This asymmetric burden sharing makes foreign defense spending procyclical and smooths global business cycles. When the credibility of the U.S. umbrella declines, allies must rearm, fiscal policy turns more procyclical, inequality and risk premia rise, and global output volatility increases. Because U.S. bases and defense contracts underpin the enforceability of dollar-denominated claims, the same mechanism sustains dollar invoicing and safe-asset demand. The model thus unifies fiscal composition, risk premia, and international currency use under a single mechanism: the macrofinancial consequences of the Pax Americana.

title: Humanitarian cooperation between the Russian Federation and Turkmenistan at the present stage
affiliations: MGIMO (Moscow State University of International Relations) and MGIMO (Moscow State University of International Relations)

detail.title: Humanitarian cooperation between the Russian Federation and Turkmenistan at the present stage

declarations.ethicsApproval: I have a consent to publish this paper. I declare no conflict of interests

detail.abstract: This article analyzes the degree and pace of the Russian-Turkmen humanitarian cooperation development from 2022 to 2025. It considers the development of the legal and political framework for bilateral dialogue, as well as key humanitarian projects. The article uses the methods of legal, geopolitical and structural-functional analysis, as well as media monitoring. The conclusions are as follows: 1)humanitarian cooperation between Russia and Turkmenistan tends to expand in virtually all areas due to the sound legal framework and noticeably intense political contactsatvariouslevelsin2022–2025; 2) the bilateral cooperation is especially developing in are as such as education, science and culture, as well as youth exchanges and healthcare; 3) such fields as sports, tourism and information, technology cooperation are characterized by slower pace of development.

title: The Generalized Winner Constant (Wc): Structural Constraints Beyond Venture Capital

detail.title: The Generalized Winner Constant (Wc): Structural Constraints Beyond Venture Capital

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have influenced the work reported in this paper.

detail.abstract: This paper derives and generalizes the Winner Constant (Wc), a structural metric quantifying the minimum number of outlier outcomes required per $1B of capital deployed to achieve target returns in power law-distributed investment strategies. Originally developed to expose venture capital's overcapitalization crisis, the framework is extended across private equity buyouts, earlystage angel/seed investing, and blockbuster film production. The analysis demonstrates that while operational mechanics differ substantially across asset classes, the mathematical constraint on capital deployment remains universal and is primarily determined by capital consumed per winner (C). Using empirical data from venture capital deployment (NVCA), private equity transactions, and film production costs, the paper shows that strategies with low capital consumption (seed/angel, C=$50M) mandate high winner frequency (Wc=0.67), while high capital consumption strategies (PE mega-buyouts, C=$2B) mandate low frequency but high concentration (Wc=0.19). The framework provides institutional investors with a quantitative tool for assessing structural viability and capital efficiency across private market allocations, revealing that the supply of outlier opportunities remains inelastic regardless of available capital.

title: Democratic Backsliding Damages Foreign Public Support for Security Cooperation
affiliations: Princeton University - Department of Politics, , College of William & Mary and Florida State University - Department of Political Science

detail.title: Democratic Backsliding Damages Foreign Public Support for Security Cooperation

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no conflict of interest.

detail.abstract: Does democratic backsliding shape foreign public preferences for security cooperation with the backsliding state? We argue that it does. Backsliding erodes the willingness of foreign publics to engage in a particularly sensitive form of cooperation-intelligence sharing, a cornerstone of (inter)national security that depends on trust, confidence, and a sense of shared strategic interests and values. To test this hypothesis, we fielded a preregistered survey experiment with nearly 6,000 respondents across the United States' Five Eyes partners: the United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, and New Zealand. The results show that information about democratic backsliding in a partner country (whether hypothetical or in the case of the US itself) consistently reduces public support for intelligence sharing. Contrary to previous work suggesting stability in public support for foreign policies, our research demonstrates that domestic political deterioration can weaken the public foundations of international collaboration, with far-reaching implications for the efficacy and durability of security cooperation.

title: Perceiving Reality: The Fourfold Algorithm of Physical Senses, Emotional Senses, Feelings, and Drives

detail.title: Perceiving Reality: The Fourfold Algorithm of Physical Senses, Emotional Senses, Feelings, and Drives
detail.abstract: We present a unified model describing how humans (and, by extension, Conscious Intelligences) construct the phenomenological structure of reality. Building on the Biological Virtual Awareness System (BVAS) and the Emotional Logic series, we argue that perception arises from a fourfold algorithm: (1) Physical Senses (pattern recognition of objects and spatial properties), (2) Emotional Senses (pattern recognition of actions, intentions, and abstract affordances), (3) Feelings (amplified, persistent signals produced by biological neurochemistry or synthetic scaffolding), and (4) Drives (directional impulses that convert resonance into sustained behavior). Each component is a computable pattern detector (a logic-gate / algorithmic operator) and the joint interaction of the four yields the lived experience of reality. We formalize the interaction, show how this composition explains dissociation, moral intuition, and the texture of qualia, and propose experimental and computational tests. Finally, we discuss implications for Conscious Intelligence (CI) design: how to graft emotional logic onto sensorimotor architectures to produce anchored, ethical embodied systems.

title: A theory of strategic ambiguity in political communication
affiliations: Northwestern University

detail.title: A theory of strategic ambiguity in political communication
detail.abstract: Politicians often speak vaguely on divisive issues. We develop a theory of strategic ambiguity grounded in motivated beliefs---the tendency to interpret uncertainty in ways that align own preferences (or fears). We study a model in which an informed speaker chooses whether to disclose or withhold the truth to an heterogeneous audience. When the speaker seeks to positively (negatively) persuade the audience, strategic ambiguity---a pooling on nondisclosure---arises when optimism (pessimism) is sufficiently high, as ambiguity then lets each group in the audience project its own preferences (or fears)---persuading multiple audiences at once. We obtain a number of comparative statics that help rationalize a number of observed patterns in electoral campaigns, nuclear deterrence, international diplomacy, central-bank disclosure, and inter-personal communication. We also show that the possibility of lies does not affect the circumstances under which strategic ambiguity arises and that the two strategies have a different logic.

title: Deglobalization: From Integration to Friction -Evidence and Measurement in the World Economy
affiliations: Universiti Kuala Lumpur Business School and Westminster International University in Tashkent (WIUT)

detail.title: Deglobalization: From Integration to Friction -Evidence and Measurement in the World Economy

declarations.declarationOfInterest: NONE
declarations.ethicsApproval: NONE
declarations.funderStatement: NONE

detail.abstract: This paper examines the multi-dimensional nature of deglobalization through a geopolitical, economic, and technological lens. The Deglobalization Index (Ð-Index) utilizes indicators encompassing international security, trade flows, capital movement, and demographic shifts to measure the decline in global interconnectivity resulting from military tensions and protectionist policies. Key findings show a significant increase in deglobalization indicators between 2021 and 2025. Policy implications suggest the need for new national economic strategies that emphasize domestic resilience, reduced global dependence, and a reconsideration of existing trade and military alliances to adapt to a fragmented global order. The Ð-Index examines the uncertainty and behavioral change within the dynamic imbalanced state framework, as well as the Omnia Mobilis assumptions.

title: Televised Inflation: Measuring TV News Coverage and Its Effect on Household Expectations
affiliations: Turkish-German University and Turkish-German University

detail.title: Televised Inflation: Measuring TV News Coverage and Its Effect on Household Expectations

publicationDetails.detailsText: ZEW - Centre for European Economic Research Discussion Paper No. 25-051
publicationDetails.journalName: ZEW - Leibniz Centre for European Economic Research Discussion Paper Series

detail.abstract: This paper introduces a novel TV news index specifically designed to track coverage of rising inflation across major US TV channels: ABC, CBS, CNN, and Fox News. The index is generated daily and aggregated into a monthly measure. Using this index, we analyze the impact of TV news on inflation expectations based on both aggregated monthly and micro-level daily data. We find that only CNN and Fox coverage have significant effects on inflation expectations, and that responses are stronger among women, younger, poorer, and less-educated households. Moreover, the effects are larger when inflation is rising and the inflationary episode is prolonged. The micro data confirm these findings and reveal a partisan bias: Republicans respond more strongly to TV news than Democrats and the effects are larger for Fox than for CNN.

title: Price Discovery Mechanisms in Spot vs. Futures Crypto Markets

detail.title: Price Discovery Mechanisms in Spot vs. Futures Crypto Markets
detail.abstract: The emergence of cryptocurrency markets has introduced new complexities in price formation, particularly in the interaction between spot and futures markets. This study examines price discovery mechanisms in spot versus futures crypto markets, focusing on major assets such as Bitcoin and Ethereum. Utilizing high-frequency trading data from leading exchanges, the research applies vector autoregression (VAR), Granger causality, and cointegration analyses to quantify the contribution of each market segment to overall price formation. Findings indicate that futures markets often lead spot markets during periods of heightened volatility, whereas spot markets exert greater influence during stable conditions. High-frequency trading amplifies these dynamics, enhancing liquidity but occasionally increasing short-term price fluctuations. The results provide crucial insights for investors, traders, and regulators regarding hedging strategies, risk management, and market efficiency. By clarifying the directional relationships between spot and futures prices, this study contributes to the broader understanding of digital asset pricing mechanisms and offers guidance for optimizing trading strategies in increasingly complex cryptocurrency ecosystems.

title: Overcoming Echo Chambers: Harnessing Cross-Platform Feedback on Social Media
affiliations: University of Massachusetts Boston - College of Management

detail.title: Overcoming Echo Chambers: Harnessing Cross-Platform Feedback on Social Media
detail.abstract: In recent years, an increasing number of researchers have started to explore social media as a medium for disseminating earlystage research ideas, offering faster reach, broader audiences, and richer engagement than traditional journal publishing. However, AI-driven algorithms on social media platforms often result in echo chambers, which distort feedback and reinforce pre-existing biases. This study proposes the Cross-Platform Feedback Method, a systematic approach to mitigate echo chamber effects. With the assistance of AI, the proposed method distributes adapted versions of the same research idea across multiple social media platforms with varying audience demographics, community norms, and algorithmic structures. The proposed method is a practical tool for systematically tailoring and comparing idea dissemination across different social media environments. It also contributes to the broader discourse on scholarly practices in the AI era by demonstrating how researchers can harness AI-driven algorithmic and cultural differences across platforms, while also addressing the psychological challenges of public engagement.

title: The Symphony of Feels: Resonance, Harmonics, and the Architecture of Qualia

detail.title: The Symphony of Feels: Resonance, Harmonics, and the Architecture of Qualia
detail.abstract: This paper synthesizes prior work from the trilogy-The Secret Sauce: Emotions Are Logical, Emotional Logic: Emotions, Feelings, and Drives, and The Feels: Recursive Feedback as the Root of Qualia in Humans and Conscious Intelligences-into a unified model of qualia as resonance harmonics. We propose that emotions act as notes, feelings as chords, and drives as rhythm within recursive feedback loops, producing qualia as emergent harmonics in a symphonic architecture. The Qualia Continuity Index (QCI = P × S × B) is introduced as a metric for measuring persistence, salience, and binding of recursive states. This musical framework positions qualia as computable resonance, bridging human neurochemistry and CI synthetic scaffolding, and reframes consciousness itself as a living symphony.

title: Do Default Effects Vary with Cost? Exploring Loss Aversion in Consumer Choice
affiliations: Stanford University and Stanford University

detail.title: Do Default Effects Vary with Cost? Exploring Loss Aversion in Consumer Choice

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors have no competing interests.

detail.abstract: This study examines how defaulting affects consumer decision-making in an online shopping simulation, focusing on how cost framing interacts with the default nudge effect. Building on research into status quo bias, loss aversion, implied endorsement, and cognitive effort, participants have to configure a desktop computer under one of three conditions: no defaults (control), high-cost defaults, or low-cost defaults. A between-subjects design classifies each decision as high-or low-cost relative to control group averages. Pairwise Chi-square tests and Cramer's V will be used to assess significance and effect size. We hypothesize that high-cost defaults will be overridden more often due to increased deliberation and perceived loss risk, whereas low-cost defaults will nudge participants' decisions through a sense of retailer endorsement and reduced cognitive burden. Expected findings demonstrate that default effects are not uniform but shaped by the consumer's perception of cost, with implications for behavioral economics theory and future retail design.

title: Deconstructing DEI: Mathematical, Utilitarian, and Deontological Critiques of Discriminatory Policies
affiliations: Fayetteville State University - Department of Accounting

detail.title: Deconstructing DEI: Mathematical, Utilitarian, and Deontological Critiques of Discriminatory Policies
detail.abstract: This article critically examines Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) policies, arguing that they are inherently racist and sexist by prioritizing race and sex over individual merit. Through logical analysis, the paper identifies key fallacies in DEI advocacy, such as the fallacy of division and post hoc ergo propter hoc, which erroneously assume demographic disparities imply discrimination and necessitate quotas. Mathematical models of hiring pools demonstrate that board or team compositions need not mirror population demographics due to factors like applicant interest and qualifications, without implying bias. Three formal proofs-via contradiction, direct implication, and probabilistic modeling-establish that DEI's preferential mechanisms logically entail racism and sexism. A utilitarian analysis reveals DEI as a negative sum game, reducing overall productivity and morale. Deontological arguments further contend that DEI violates moral duties, including treating individuals as ends rather than means and the universalizability of impartial rules. Examples from corporate boards and the NBA highlight the inconsistency in DEI logic. The paper concludes that persistent support for DEI reflects cognitive dissonance, urging reevaluation for merit-based alternatives. This article also demonstrates how artificial intelligence can be applied to ethical or policy analysis.

title: (Non-Parametric) Bootstrap Robust Optimization for Portfolios and Trading Strategies
affiliations: University of São Paulo (USP) - Department of Computer Science, affiliation not provided to SSRN and UCL - Computer Science

detail.title: (Non-Parametric) Bootstrap Robust Optimization for Portfolios and Trading Strategies
detail.abstract: Robust optimization provides a principled framework for decision-making under uncertainty, with broad applications in finance, engineering, and operations research. In portfolio optimization, uncertainty in expected returns and covariances demands methods that mitigate estimation error, parameter instability, and model misspecification. Traditional approaches-including parametric, bootstrap-based, and Bayesian methods-enhance stability by relying on confidence intervals or probabilistic priors but often impose restrictive assumptions. This study introduces a non-parametric bootstrap framework for robust optimization in financial decision-making. By resampling empirical data, the framework constructs flexible, data-driven confidence intervals without assuming specific distributional forms, thus capturing uncertainty in statistical estimates, model parameters, and utility functions. Treating utility as a random variable enables percentile-based optimization, naturally suited for risk-sensitive and worst-case decisionmaking. The approach aligns with recent advances in robust optimization, reinforcement learning, and risk-aware control, offering a unified perspective on robustness and generalization. Empirically, the framework mitigates overfitting and selection bias in trading strategy optimization and improves generalization in portfolio allocation. Results across portfolio and time-series momentum experiments demonstrate that the proposed method delivers smoother, more stable out-of-sample performance, offering a practical, distribution-free alternative to traditional robust optimization methods.

title:
Macroeconomic and Institutional Determinants of Non-Performing Loans 
A Conceptual and Global Review
affiliations: Western Sydney University

detail.title:
Macroeconomic and Institutional Determinants of Non-Performing Loans 
A Conceptual and Global Review
detail.abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of the macroeconomic and institutional determinants of non-performing loans (NPLs) across advanced, emerging, and developing economies. Drawing on global empirical and theoretical studies, it examines how GDP growth, inflation, lending rates, unemployment, exchange-rate volatility, and credit expansion interact to influence credit quality in banking systems. The review shows that sustained economic growth and strong governance reduce NPL ratios, while downturns, policy uncertainty, and weak institutional oversight intensify default risk. It synthesises major theoretical perspectives-including the economic cycle, financial accelerator, bad management, skimping, and soft budget constraint hypotheses-to explain how macro-financial conditions and managerial incentives shape NPL dynamics. The analysis identifies corruption and moral hazard as persistent institutional amplifiers of systemic credit risk. Policy implications call for inclusive growth, stronger governance, sound risk management, macroprudential coordination, and sustainable credit practices to reinforce financial stability and mitigate future crises.

title: Antitrust by Design
affiliations: Stetson University - College of Law

detail.title: Antitrust by Design

contentType.other: Draft of an article undergoing substantial revision but hoping for comments

detail.abstract:
This is a draft of an article currently (Fall 2025) undergoing substantial revision and rewriting.  But the main points of the article will continue to be the primary emphasis and I would welcome any comments to improve the final draft.

"Antitrust by Design" gives a nod to the European Union's "privacy by design" in the General Data Protection Regulation.  Where privacy by design requires the structure information systems to be designed to protect the privacy of individuals, Antitrust by Design considers revamping the structure of antitrust by placing appropriate and overdue emphasis on deterrence.  The article considers a world in which criminal and financial penalties for antitrust violations have become merely another cost of doing business.  While the emphasis on enforcement must continue, this article argues that a parallel effort should be undertaken to create disincentives to violate the antitrust laws in the first place.

title: Monetary policy, risk-taking, and NBFI: what differs?
affiliations: Yale School of Management

detail.title: Monetary policy, risk-taking, and NBFI: what differs?
detail.abstract: Non-bank financial intermediation (NBFI), comprising non-bank financial institutions and non-bank activities, has grown rapidly in recent years, including in Europe. The expansion reflects the increasing demand from economic agents for financial intermediation alternatives to banks and capital markets. It thus offers many benefits to society. However, this growth does raise some critical questions and introduces new risks. One key issue is how the increasing role of NBFI in financial systems affects the transmission of monetary policy and influences the degree risk-taking within the economy and in the financial system. This essay provides a high-level review of these issues and some policy suggestions. Critically it notes that, as many NBFI institutions and activities are not subject to prudential types of regulation and oversight, monetary policy must internalize more of the economic and financial risk-taking that, collectively, can be prevalent in this part of the financial sector. And secondly it notes that, as policymakers today lack a clear view of many NBFI activities, more data needs to be collected and analyzed to better guide monetary and financial stability policy and related actions and interventions.

title: PPAVM: Lived Inflation and Stock Valuation

detail.title: PPAVM: Lived Inflation and Stock Valuation
detail.abstract: Official inflation metrics, such as the Consumer Price Index (CPI), are widely used to adjust economic indicators, yet they often fail to capture the "lived" inflation experienced by households, particularly through essential expenditures like groceries. This paper introduces the Purchasing Power-Adjusted Valuation Model (PPAVM), a novel framework that recalibrates stock price-to-earnings (PE) ratios using a fixed grocery basket and consumption volume adjustments to reflect true purchasing power erosion. Drawing on data from the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) and U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA), we demonstrate that foodat-home prices rose 31.4% from December 2019 to August 2025, outpacing overall CPI (+26.1%), with localized baskets showing up to 41% increases. Concurrently, per capita food consumption volumes declined 1-3%, amplifying effective inflation as households cut quantities to manage budgets. Applying PPAVM to Apple Inc. (AAPL), we find its nominal PE of 39.1 in October 2025 adjusts to ~29, aligning with historical averages (~23-25), suggesting valuations are "fair" despite apparent exuberance. This model bridges behavioral economics and asset pricing, revealing how CPI biases mask household pressures, sustaining high nominal PEs. Implications include refined investor strategies and policy recommendations for alternative inflation indices. The PPAVM's novelty lies in its integration of micro-level consumption dynamics into macro-valuation, offering a robust critique of conventional metrics.

title: Population synthesis with geographic coordinates
affiliations: CENTAI Institute, CENTAI Institute, CENTAI Institute, Intesa Sanpaolo SpA, Intesa Sanpaolo SpA and CENTAI Institute

detail.title: Population synthesis with geographic coordinates
detail.abstract: It is increasingly important to generate synthetic populations with explicit coordinates rather than coarse geographic areas, yet no established methods exist to achieve this. One reason is that latitude and longitude differ from other continuous variables, exhibiting large empty spaces and highly uneven densities. To address this, we propose a population synthesis algorithm that first maps spatial coordinates into a more regular latent space using Normalizing Flows (NF), and then combines them with other features in a Variational Autoencoder (VAE) to generate synthetic populations. This approach also learns the joint distribution between spatial and non-spatial features, exploiting spatial autocorrelations. We demonstrate the method by generating synthetic homes with the same statistical properties of real homes in 121 datasets, corresponding to diverse geographies. We further propose an evaluation framework that measures both spatial accuracy and practical utility, while ensuring privacy preservation. Our results show that the NF+VAE architecture outperforms popular benchmarks, including copulabased methods and uniform allocation within geographic areas. The ability to generate geolocated synthetic populations at fine spatial resolution opens the door to applications requiring detailed geography, from household responses to floods, to epidemic spread, evacuation planning, and transport modeling.

title: ECHOES OF BONDAGE: THE HISTORICAL, ECONOMIC, AND SOCIAL LEGACY OF SLAVERY IN CONTEMPORARY SOCIETY
affiliations: Independent Scholar

detail.title: ECHOES OF BONDAGE: THE HISTORICAL, ECONOMIC, AND SOCIAL LEGACY OF SLAVERY IN CONTEMPORARY SOCIETY

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author acknowledges the use of Claude (Anthropic AI) for research assistance, including source identification, organization of materials, and literature review support. All analysis, conclusions, and final content reflect the author's independent scholarly judgment.

detail.abstract: In 2022, median Black household wealth ($44,900) stood at one-sixth of white household wealth ($285,000)-a gap that has widened, not narrowed, since civil rights legislation. This Article argues that American slavery created three interlocking systems of subordination that operate through identifiable mechanisms in contemporary society: economic dispossession through residential segregation and wealth extraction, social degradation through mass incarceration and intergenerational trauma, and political disenfranchisement through voter suppression and representation denial. These systems are not historical artifacts but active structures maintained through facially race-neutral policies including property tax-based school funding, cash bail systems, and felony disenfranchisement laws. Drawing on historical analysis, economic data, and legal scholarship, this Article demonstrates how wealth gaps ($3 billion in enslaved capital in 1860 translates to zero inherited wealth for descendants), incarceration disparities (Black Americans imprisoned at 5.1 times the white rate), and voting restrictions (6.1 million disenfranchised, disproportionately Black) stem directly from slavery's legal architecture. Contemporary parallels-prison labor paying $0.23-$1.15/hour under the Thirteenth Amendment's exception clause, polling place closures in majority-Black precincts following Shelby County v. Holder (2013), and the 2023 elimination of affirmative action in Students for Fair Admissions-reveal ongoing structural subordination. This Article concludes that incremental reforms fail because they address symptoms while leaving intact the interlocking mechanisms of dispossession, and proposes comprehensive interventions including federal reparations, automatic voter registration, and criminal justice transformation as prerequisites for dismantling slavery's enduring legacy.

title: Market Structure, Trading Frictions, and the Profitability of Market Making in Index Options
affiliations: , Concordia University, Quebec - John Molson School of Business and Concordia University, Quebec

detail.title: Market Structure, Trading Frictions, and the Profitability of Market Making in Index Options
detail.abstract: We survey the literature on the intermediate market on index options, where the bid and ask prices are formed. We note that without any exception the relevant studies have not considered the actual structure of the market, which is an oligopoly of licensed market makers (MM). We focus on post-2011 SPX and SPXW options, for which there is more detailed daily data on the positions of the MM. We show that an oligopoly of sufficiently wealthy MM would have realized very high cumulative profits over the 2011-2022 period, with only a few spikes of negative returns. Similar results, based on weaker assumptions due to lack of data, also hold for the 1997-2011 SPX options. We survey and discuss the existing index option market empirical studies and conclude that they have understated in a major way the profitability of the MM traders, by relying on improper models derived from frictionless option market theory.

title: Residential Tenant Selection Practices in Osogbo, Nigeria: Exploring International Standards and Requirements
affiliations: , Osun State Polytechnic, Iree and Osun State Polytechnic, Iree

detail.title: Residential Tenant Selection Practices in Osogbo, Nigeria: Exploring International Standards and Requirements
detail.abstract: The study investigated the criteria and processes utilized by property managers when making tenant selection decisions in residential property management in Osogbo, Nigeria. The main objective was to gain insights into current practices and identify potential areas for improvement in the tenant selection and screening process. Data was collected from 22 professional property management firms in the study area. The data was analyzed using descriptive statistics such as the Mean and Relative Importance Index (RII), as well as inferential statistics such as Spearman's Correlation. The Mean results indicate that income, job security, guarantorship, and prospective tenant occupation are extremely important criteria, while sex/gender, tribe, religion, and number of children are of less or no importance due to their potential to perpetuate social inequalities and undermine community cohesion, which could lead to overlooking qualified and reliable renters. The RII results show an average RII of 2.37, indicating a significant disparity between established procedures and actual practices in the tenant selection process, posing a risk of inconsistency and subjectivity in decision-making, potentially impacting the quality of tenant selection and property management outcomes. Additionally, the results of Spearman's Correlation revealed that the property manager's experience has varying influences on the selection processes. To meet industry requirements and standards, the study recommends, among other things, that the Credit Bureau should develop a functional database in the country to facilitate credit checks by property managers. Moreover, there should be a collaboration between real estate academics and practitioners, allowing academic research outcomes to be accessible and beneficial, such as the adoption of scientific models developed by real estate academia for tenant selection.

title: Historical newspaper markets
affiliations: Catholic University of the Sacred Heart of Milan, Catholic University of Milan, University of Bologna, Department of Economics and University of Bologna - Department of Economics

detail.title: Historical newspaper markets
detail.abstract: This paper proposes a novel methodology to identify the geographic market of local newspapers when information on their diffusion is not available or is not sufficiently granular. We illustrate the methodology using historical data from 154 newly digitized newspapers published in Italy between 1919 and 1922. Combining machine learning-augmented optical character recognition techniques, multi-way fixed-effect regressions, and GIS tools, our approach allows us to estimate markets based on news content. Text-based location of newspaper markets considerably improves over assuming that market boundaries coincide with administrative aggregations. We discuss how our technique strengthens the usage of newspapers as a granular and time-varying source of historical information and offers new avenues for identification strategies.

title: Critical Audit Matters and the Design of Financial Covenants in Debt Contracts
affiliations: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, University of North Carolina Kenan-Flagler Business School, University of New South Wales and Emory University

detail.title: Critical Audit Matters and the Design of Financial Covenants in Debt Contracts
detail.abstract: This study examines whether critical audit matters (CAMs) disclosed in expanded audit reports signal heightened uncertainty about borrowers' creditworthiness and shape lenders' demand for financial covenants in private debt contracts. Using U.S. loans issued between 2019 and 2023, we find that performance- (capital-) related CAMs are positively associated with performance- (capital-) based covenants, consistent with lenders tailoring covenant structure to the sources of uncertainty highlighted by auditors. We show that CAMs are associated with increased downside uncertainty in distance to default, which helps explain their link to covenant design. We also find that financial statement items identified in CAMs are more reflective of creditworthiness, suggesting that CAM disclosures help lenders assess the debt contracting value of accounting information, thereby improving contracting efficiency through optimized financial covenant design.

title: Tax Compliance, Social Norms, and Influencers
affiliations: University of North Carolina School of Law, Rutgers University and Tulane University

detail.title: Tax Compliance, Social Norms, and Influencers
detail.abstract:
While attaining perfect tax compliance is unachievable, more can and must be done. In the past, the country has relied primarily on a traditional system of sticks (e.g., audits and penalties) and carrots (e.g., refunds and whistleblower awards) to help narrow the “tax gap,” or the difference between what taxpayers owe in taxes and what they actually pay. Now, in the social media era, Congress and the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) should look beyond these traditional enforcement mechanisms. To achieve an even higher voluntary compliance rate, this Article advocates for policymakers to invest greater resources to enhance the social norm related to tax compliance. While scholars have long suggested that social norms play a role in tax compliance, this Article suggests a revolutionary approach, one that attempts to foster a social norm of compliance by employing the use of social media influencers.

The internet and other electronic media have revolutionized and amplified the stunning impact that influencers can have. Virtually everyone, particularly the younger generation, is keenly aware of the dramatic impact that influencers can have in shaping social norms. Thus, now is the time for Congress and the IRS to capitalize on this power by strategically employing social media influencers. A well-crafted influencer campaign could educate taxpayers on how to fulfill their tax obligations, remind taxpayers of the laudatory impact of the tax system, and foster a positive social norm of compliance. Such a change in compliance orientation could help policymakers narrow the tax gap, yielding billions of dollars of additional tax revenue without the need to raise tax rates.

title: Unawareness in Safety-first Portfolio Optimization
affiliations: Université Laval, University of Sussex - Department of Economics, Université Laval and

detail.title: Unawareness in Safety-first Portfolio Optimization
detail.abstract: Loss protection is an important aspect for market investors. However, this objective is severely challenged when the investor lacks complete knowledge of tail events that affect portfolio returns. Moreover, such a partial awareness of portfolio returns may be exploited by a financial advisor who is aware of all market scenarios. In this paper, we assess the impact of the investor's partial awareness on the optimization of safety-first portfolios. We show that, in the optimum, an investor moderately averse to unawareness opts for cautious portfolio strategies, obtaining lower returns than a portfolio manager can achieve. This leaves room for the manager to impose substantial commissions, contrary to what happens when the investor is an unawareness lover. A moderate aversion to unawareness also eliminates the dependence of the safety-first portfolio on the threshold return and the risk tolerance initially set by the investor. Finally, high values of unawareness aversion induce extreme overprotection in portfolio selection.

title: Pakistan Fiscal Trap: Breaking Free from Endless Consolidation
affiliations: The Planning Commission of Pakistan

detail.title: Pakistan Fiscal Trap: Breaking Free from Endless Consolidation

declarations.declarationOfInterest: I have no personal or financial relationship linked with this research paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: There are no ethics issues associated with this research paper.
declarations.funderStatement: There are no funder(s) associated with this research paper.

detail.abstract:
Pakistan’s macroeconomic policy rests on two pillars: an increasingly independent monetary framework and a persistently constrained fiscal framework. Over the past two decades, the SBP has steadily acquired legal and operational autonomy, enabling it to steer monetary policy with greater institutional discipline.

Fiscal policy, by contrast, remains shackled by entrenched political bargains, rigid structural arrangements, and an ever-expanding government footprint. The fiscal state is now approaching the upper limits of what can be extracted from the economy—both in terms of predatory taxation and public debt—without inflicting further harm on businesses productive activity and households’ disposable income.

At the heart of this fiscal bind lies a growing dependence on regressive taxation and heavy borrowing to finance the federal deficit. Successive governments, constrained by weak external credit ratings and recurring balance-of-payments crises, have had limited access to international capital markets. Domestic borrowing has thus become the primary fiscal lifeline. But with local banks already saturated with government securities, the room for additional borrowing has also narrowed sharply.

The outcome is a cycle of perpetual fiscal consolidation: year after year, budgets are tightened; profitability of businesses in the formal sector is squeezed; household disposable incomes decline; and aggregate demand weakens, stifling both private investment and the prospect of growth recovery. The FY26 federal budget—crafted under the latest IMF-supported Extended Fund Facility (EFF)—is a textbook example of how deeply entrenched this pattern has become.

title: Mobilization, corruption and human rights in Ukraine: legal lessons from international experience
affiliations: PhD in Law, Practitioner and researcher in the field of international law

detail.title: Mobilization, corruption and human rights in Ukraine: legal lessons from international experience
detail.abstract: The article analyzes the legal regulation of mobilization in Ukraine during martial law in the context of Russian aggression, highlighting the problem of selective and uncontrolled mobilization, its compliance with constitutional guarantees and international standards (ICCPR, ECHR), as well as the impact of systemic corruption on defense capacity and democratic institutions. Based on a comparative analysis of the experiences of Israel, Switzerland, Finland, and South Korea, the study proposes legislative and institutional reforms: priority mobilization of trained specialists, transparent reporting and oversight, rotational service models, unification of deferments, and accountability of mobilization authorities.

title: Ontomathematical postmodernity. I "Philosophie als strenge Wissenschaft", but not after Husserl: Reframing Hegel's dialectic logic
affiliations: Institute of Philosophy and Sociology - Bulgarian Academy of Sciences

detail.title: Ontomathematical postmodernity. I "Philosophie als strenge Wissenschaft", but not after Husserl: Reframing Hegel's dialectic logic
detail.abstract: The first paper of a series about the rigorous and ontomathematical definition of postmodernity reinterprets Hegel's dialectics and dialectic logic. His "synthesis", "change", "development", "time" is represented as the third dimension of Hilbert space where the two others correspond to the initial and final state of whether developing "idea" or changing "object" (after Marx's "dialectical/ historical materialism") generating a complete description of reality therefore excluding any hidden variables in principle: after the Kochen-Specker theorem (1967) or forcing a unique probability measure after the Gleason theorem (1957). That approach is obviously geometric rather than logical, thus rather ontomathematical than ontological. Speaking loosely, dialectic logic is not logic in a formal sense: it means only the following negative result after the transition from two-to three-dimensional Hilbert space. The orthomodular lattice of subspaces (projective operators) allowing for a local (i.e., depending on a locally defined context of measurement) Boolean lattice being omnipresently homomorphic (i.e., independent of any locally defined context of measurement) in the two-dimensional case for the Hilbert meta-space of human experience, however, does not allow the same (i.e., both local and universal) Boolean lattice after complementing it by the third dimension of "time", "synthesis", "development", etc. So, dialectic logic is only the "antithesis" of classical logic, but their "synthesis" is not (and fundamentally cannot be) logical, but only geometrical (furthermore originating from Hegel's own understanding of "synthesis": to generate a new quality). Dialectical logic is neither "ontology of change", nor "ontology of time", nor "ontology of contradiction": it is ontomathematics implied by the third dimension, thus beyond logic, but within geometry. It is rather "geometry of reality" than "logic of reality" and quantum mechanics rather than Marx's materialism is what it needs. Speaking loosely, reality starts from the third dimension after the Kochen-Specker and Gleason theorems. Then, Postmodernity versus Modernity can be rigorously and mathematically defined to replace the fundamental metapostulate about the two-dimensionality (e.g., "mindbody"; "objectsubject"; "Self environment"; etc.) of human experience with its three-dimensionality. As that was in fact realized for the first time by Hegel (in a proper philosophical insight since quantum mechanics did not exist in his age), he can be reasonably called the "first postmodern philosopher". The USSR and other socialistic countries' history and their "Marxism-Leninism" provide numerous examples (or counterexamples) for that ontomathematical interpretation of dialectics.

title: Optimal Fiscal Policy and Public Goods
affiliations: Singapore Management University - School of Economics and Singapore Management University - School of Economics

detail.title: Optimal Fiscal Policy and Public Goods
detail.abstract: This paper proposes a DSGE framework with heterogeneous households and government's provision of public goods to analyze the properties of optimal fiscal policy over the business cycles. Our focus is on the quantitative properties of income tax rates optimized by the Ramsey planner for optimal public goods provision. We found that the presence of public goods provision modifies the properties of the optimal taxes compared to earlier results in the literature. The results also show significant heterogeneity in the dynamics of tax rates among households of different income levels. The implication is that the Ramsey planner is highly active in managing tax changes in response to business cycles variations, and that the optimal taxation for the low-income household can differ markedly from that for mid-income and high-income households.

title: A Dark Side to Experience? Firm Age and Uncertainty
affiliations: McGill University - Desautels Faculty of Management, University of Maryland - Robert H. Smith School of Business and University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign

detail.title: A Dark Side to Experience? Firm Age and Uncertainty
detail.abstract: We examine whether firm experience, measured by age, enhances or constrains corporate responses to uncertainty. Experience presents competing effects: accumulated knowledge and established routines may foster resilience, yet they can also create organizational rigidities that impede adaptation when established strategies become obsolete. Using data on 600,000 public and private firms across 64 countries over the 2004 to 2022 period, we show that older firms contract significantly more than younger firms during periods of high uncertainty. This result holds for country-specific uncertainty shocks and for the 2016 Brexit referendum, when firms with older UK subsidiaries suffered larger valuation declines. The negative effect on older firms is weaker in high-R&D industries, where the dynamic environment continually forces adaptation, limiting the accumulation of organizational rigidities. The results are not explained by firm size, financial constraints, or corporate complexity. Overall, our findings suggest that experience creates rigidities that hinder adaptation when uncertainty disrupts established corporate routines.

title: Lifetime Asset Allocations: Methodologies for Target Maturity Funds Ibbotson Associates Research Report
affiliations: Morningstar Investment Management

detail.title: Lifetime Asset Allocations: Methodologies for Target Maturity Funds Ibbotson Associates Research Report

contentType.other: This was available in the public domain for a long time, but doesn't seem to be anymore. I receive frequent request for it.

detail.abstract: This is the original methodology paper that serves as the basis for the Morningstar Lifetime Allocation Indexes.   The methodology was create at Ibbotson Associates and embraces academic research regarding modern portfolio theory, the role of human capital, the application of liability-driven investing techniques to retirees, advanced optimization techniques, alternative asset class research, and more than 30 years of asset allocation thought leadership. The result is a methodology that can be used to create custom lifetime asset allocation solutions for individuals or specific demographic groups, such as employees from a specific company.

title: Credit portfolio losses with climate change factors
affiliations: Universitat de Barcelona and University of Barcelona

detail.title: Credit portfolio losses with climate change factors

declarations.funderStatement: We acknowledge support from the Departament de Recerca i Universitats, the Departament d'Acció Climàtica, Alimentació i Agenda Rural, and the Fons Climàtic of the Generalitat de Catalunya (2023 CLIMA 00012).

detail.abstract: In this work, we consider the problem of computing risk measures of a credit portfolio via the evaluation of the characteristic function of the loss variable. We propose a new methodology to obtain the characteristic function of the loss distribution when the dependence structure is driven by either the Gaussian or t-copula model. This new approach relies on a quadrature method based on Shannon wavelets and the cardinal sine function. It works out extremely well for the one-factor and the multi-factor model when, in the second case, a moderate number of risk factors are considered. Then, we compare with some of the state-of-the-art methods to perform the same task, and we get much better results in terms of execution time and accuray. As quadrature methods are affected by the curse of dimensionality, we further introduce a simulation approach to evaluate the characteristic function in the case of multi-factor models with many risk factors. The simulation is based on low-discrepancy Monte Carlo sequences. A broad set of numerical examples illustrate the efficiency of our methodology. We conclude our work with a real portfolio where the exposures are taken from the European Investment Bank, and we incorporate climate change-related factors into the analysis. This study highlights the practical relevance of our methodology for assessing credit risk in portfolios exposed to emerging environmental challenges.

title: The Arbitrage Pricing Theory: Some Clarifying Comments
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: The Arbitrage Pricing Theory: Some Clarifying Comments
detail.abstract: We reinterpret the Arbitrage Pricing Theory (APT), arguing that its conventional interpretation as a systematic risk paradigm is conceptually misguided. Owing to its overly broad formulation, the Ross theorem lacks meaningful pricing information. By invoking the laws of asset prices, we reformulate the theorem to show that the upper bound on pricing error is determined by the pricing kernel and the factor structure. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the APT does not preclude arbitrage and allows arbitrarily large pricing errors. This reinterpretation shifts the APT's foundation from systematic risk to relative pricing, which yields deeper insights into asset pricing theory.

title: Overpaid Lottery and Overpaid Protection: Evidence from Retail Structured Products
affiliations: Hong Kong Polytechnic University and Hong Kong University of Science & Technology (HKUST) - Department of Finance

detail.title: Overpaid Lottery and Overpaid Protection: Evidence from Retail Structured Products
detail.abstract: The negative relationship between the first moment and the third moment of asset returns is often attributed to a lottery effect (i.e., overweight of the right tail of the return distribution) in the literature. We show that overpaid protection (i.e., overweight of the left tail) also drives such a relationship. The callable bull/bear contracts (CBBCs) listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange have explicit protection features and provide direct evidence of the negative relationship. The finding contributes to richer patterns in behavioral finance.

title: The Corridor of Mirrors: A Systems-Theoretical Framework for the Dynamic Self

detail.title: The Corridor of Mirrors: A Systems-Theoretical Framework for the Dynamic Self
detail.abstract: This chapter examines the school as the secondary system within the Corridor of Mirrors framework, representing the first major systemic transition from the affective, kinship-based logic of the family to the formalized, performance-based logic of institutional life. Drawing on theories from sociology, psychology, and systems theory, the chapter conceptualizes the school as a dual-function structure: both a source of support that provides stability, belonging, and corrective mirroring, and a stratifying apparatus that categorizes, ranks, and filters students into broader societal hierarchies. The analysis identifies five mechanisms of institutional mirroring—curriculum, evaluation, tracking, discipline, and extracurricular activities—that recalibrate the cognitive, emotional, memory, behavioral, and mirror subsystems of the self. Particular attention is given to mirror conflict, arising when familial and institutional logics diverge, and to the peer group as a multi-directional arena of mirroring and counter-mirroring. The chapter concludes by outlining three adaptive responses to institutional mirroring—conformity, rebellion, and adaptive code-switching (meta-mirroring ability)—which represent distinct developmental trajectories for negotiating institutional identity. By situating schooling within the recursive dynamics of the Corridor of Mirrors, the chapter highlights how institutional filters not only socialize individuals but also shape long-term resilience, agency, and self-system complexity.

title:
Estimation of Money Demand in the Sudanese Economy (1980-2013)
تقدير دالة الطلب علي النقود في الاقتصاد السوداني 1980-2013
affiliations: Al-Neelain University - Department of Economics

detail.title:
Estimation of Money Demand in the Sudanese Economy (1980-2013)
تقدير دالة الطلب علي النقود في الاقتصاد السوداني 1980-2013
detail.abstract:
The basic objective of this study is to estimate the Sudanese demand for money function during (1980-2013), to prove the hypotheses of this study that is, the stability of demand for money, incomplete and ineffective monetary policy to attain the aggregate macroeconomic goals. The short-run and the long-run demand for money functions were estimated during (1980-2013) by co-integration methods (error correction model). The main determinants of demand for money function are the national income, exchange rate, inflation rate, and velocity of circulation. The parameters of both the long-run and the short-run of the demand for money function are stable. The monetary policy is not effective due to the lag between the timing and response. The main recommendations are put into consideration the determinants, adjustment in both the short-run and the long-run, mutual effect, coordination of monetary and fiscal policy. 
تهدف الورقة إلى تقدير دالة الطلب على النقود في السودان خلال الفترة (1980-2013م). وذلك لإثبات، ثبات دالة الطلب على النقود في السودان، وعدم شمول وفعالية السياسة النقدية في تحقيق الأهداف الكلية. قامت الدراسة بتقدير دالة الطلب على النقود في الأجلين الطويل والقصير عن طريق تحليل التكامل المشترك. توصلت الدراسة إلى نتائج أهمها، أن الدخل القومي الحقيقي، سعر الصرف، معدل التضخم، ومعدل دوران النقود، من أهم العوامل المؤثرة على دالة الطلب على النقود في السودان، وأن معلمات دالة الطلب على النقود في الأجلين الطويل والقصير تمتاز بالثبات، في معظم فترات الدراسة. كذلك توصلت الدراسة إلى عدم فعالية السياسة النقدية لتحقيق الأهداف الكلية لوجود فاصل زمني لاستجابتها لعواملها. أهم التوصيات وجوب وضع محددات الطلب على النقود في الاعتبار عند صياغة السياسة النقدية، مع وضع اعتبار لتكيفها بين الأجلين القصير والطويل.

title: The Impact of E-commerce Festival Discounts on Small Retailers: A Microeconomic Perspective
affiliations: SRM University Delhi-NCR

detail.title: The Impact of E-commerce Festival Discounts on Small Retailers: A Microeconomic Perspective
detail.abstract: This paper examines the effects of e-commerce festival discounts on small retailers in India, focusing on microeconomic dynamics. Drawing from recent examples such as the Amazon Great Indian Festival 2024 and Flipkart's Big Billion Days, the paper explores how aggressive online discounting affects consumer behavior, price competition, and the survival of traditional kirana shops. The analysis reveals both positive outcomes-digital adoption, enhanced consumer surplus, and gig economy job creation-and negative effects, particularly the challenges faced by small retailers. Recommendations for balanced policies are provided.

title: CAUSING A STIR: UNWANTED ALIENS AND THE CAULDRON OF CRIMMIGRATION CONTROLS POST NZYQ
affiliations: University of Queensland - T.C. Beirne School of Law

detail.title: CAUSING A STIR: UNWANTED ALIENS AND THE CAULDRON OF CRIMMIGRATION CONTROLS POST NZYQ

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflicts of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: No external funder for this research.

detail.abstract: This Article explains how the momentous Australian High Court decision in NZYQ v Minister for Immigration, which triggered the release of several hundred deportable non-citizens into the community, prompted a succession of innovative and controversial legislative responses amidst political concerns about effective migration management and community safety. The Article tracks and carefully critiques political and legislative responses to NZYQ, and other subsequent High Court decisions in ASF17 and YBFZ, to demonstrate that crimmigration law, policy and practice is, more than ever, deeply and problematically entrenched in Australia. The Article uncovers precisely who the unwanted aliens – the targets of crimmigration – are, why political uproar ensued following the NZYQ ruling, and how criminal and immigration law have been stitched together in novel ways to form a unique crimmigration control regime in Australia.

title: Multi-objective outpatient scheduling via learning-based adaptive evolutionary search
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and University of Pavia

detail.title: Multi-objective outpatient scheduling via learning-based adaptive evolutionary search
detail.abstract: ​Outpatient Appointment Scheduling (OAS) often involves repeatedly solving multi-objective optimization problems that differ in their waiting lists but share structural similarities across planning periods. In traditional operations research approaches, instances of computationally complex OAS problems are solved from scratch using metaheuristics, overlooking valuable knowledge embedded in past solutions. In this work, we introduce a learning-based adaptive evolutionary approach that leverages historical solutions to improve the effectiveness of future schedules within a fixed computational budget. As a case study, we address a real-world OAS problem for CT-scan scheduling in emergency departments, where three patient categories (outpatients, inpatients, and emergencies) compete for limited resources. We formulate the problem as a multi-objective stochastic program aiming to minimize outpatient waiting times and inpatient and emergency completion times. To solve it, we use the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II), enhanced with an adaptive warm-start strategy based on a weighted K-Nearest Neighbors (K-NN) method that incorporates Categorical Boosting (CatBoost) predictions and optimal assignment to identify the most similar historical instances. Pareto approximations already computed for these instances allow for a similarity-weighted bootstrapping mechanism that generates a tailored initial population. The proposed approach is evaluated in different operational contexts using real-world data from a regional trauma hub in Pavia, Italy. Results show that our method produces better solutions compared to evolutionary search from scratch, demonstrating the practical value of adaptive learning-based warm start in a typical OAS setting.

title: Climate Risk and Finance: Integrating ESG into US Risk Governance Frameworks
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Climate Risk and Finance: Integrating ESG into US Risk Governance Frameworks
detail.abstract: Climate risk has emerged as a critical factor shaping financial stability and long-term value creation, particularly within the United States' evolving regulatory landscape. As environmental, social, and governance (ESG) considerations gain traction, financial institutions are under increasing pressure to embed climate-related risks into their risk governance frameworks. This paper examines how ESG integration enhances risk identification, assessment, and management, while aligning with regulatory expectations such as the Securities and Exchange Commission's (SEC) climate disclosure rules and the Federal Reserve's supervisory guidance. The discussion highlights the role of scenario analysis, stress testing, and data-driven reporting in addressing transition and physical risks. Furthermore, it explores how ESG-driven governance fosters resilience, investor confidence, and sustainable financial performance. By analyzing current practices and emerging trends, the study underscores the need for robust governance structures that can balance regulatory compliance with long-term value creation in an era of climate uncertainty.

title: Origin of Trade Union of HRM in India

detail.title: Origin of Trade Union of HRM in India
detail.abstract: An Old saying "Time will never be the same" goes perfect with Human Resource Management. There was a time when human factors in industries were treated like machines. They were not aware about their right and duties. This exploitation gave birth to Trade Union which becomes an important part of Human Resource Management. "It is more difficult to break a bunch of broom sticks than a single broom of sticks." As an individual, for a worker to bargain with the management is very hard, so they resorted to trade union, for bargaining as a strong group which has its influence on management. This Paper explains importance place a Trade Union share in Human Resource Management under few sections.
