title: Cultural Convergence or Cultural Erosion? A Critical Qualitative Analysis of Western Media's Influence on Youth Identity, Lifestyle, and Social Norms in Pakistan

detail.title: Cultural Convergence or Cultural Erosion? A Critical Qualitative Analysis of Western Media's Influence on Youth Identity, Lifestyle, and Social Norms in Pakistan

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Non
declarations.ethicsApproval: Non
declarations.funderStatement: Non

detail.abstract: The growing influence of the Western media in Pakistan poses serious questions concerning the role of youth identity transformation: Is the introduction of global cultural flows to the Pakistani youth part of the cultural convergence or cultural destruction? This is a qualitative work where the use of interpretative phenomenological analysis (IPA) is utilized by examining how the Pakistani young adults iron out the role of Western media in shaping their identity, their way of life as well as their social constructs. These aspects of acculturation are subtle and rarely captured in popular press coverage; using semistructured interviewing with 20 respondents in urban and semi-urban communities in the greater New Orleans area, there are particular nuances of acculturation that include selective use of Western practices and strengthening of local traditions. Results highlight the emergence of hybrid identities that are formed through cultural homogenization, resistance, and glocalization at the same time. By placing the Pakistani youth in a larger discourse of globalization, hybridity and postcolonial identity, this study focuses on youth agency in cultural negotiation. Relevance demonstrates the significance of media literacy programs with culturally based appeal, curriculum revision, and policy advocacy.

reference: 57 St. Mary's Law Journal 77 (2025)
title: Transcending Tradition Through Inclusive Online Pedagogy
affiliations: Florida A&M University College of Law

detail.title: Transcending Tradition Through Inclusive Online Pedagogy

publicationDetails.detailsText: 57 St. Mary's Law Journal 77 (2025)

detail.abstract:
This work critiques the exclusionary nature of the traditional Socratic method and introduces The New Pedagogy: Online Socrates as a foundational framework for building more inclusive, equitable, and student-centered approaches to legal education.

It challenges the continued reliance on the traditional Socratic method in legal education, arguing that its hierarchical and exclusionary nature undermines meaningful inclusion and student engagement—both online and in the classroom. It contends that the barriers often attributed to online learning expose deeper inequities within traditional legal pedagogy itself.

Building on this critique, the work proposes that the shift to online education provides a unique opportunity to transcend tradition by developing intentionally inclusive, collaborative, and student-centered approaches to teaching law. It introduces the foundational concept of The New Pedagogy: Online Socrates, which begins the work of reimagining the rigor of Socratic dialogue through practices that promote equity, belonging, and accessibility. This conceptual framing lays the groundwork for further development of The New Pedagogy: Online Socrates in future scholarship and envisions a more just and inclusive model for legal education.

title: Evaluation of New Zealand's Named Patient Pharmaceutical Assessment Scheme: Citation Analysis, Document Review, Performance Metrics, and Media Perception Author
affiliations: Victoria University of Wellington - Te Herenga Waka

detail.title: Evaluation of New Zealand's Named Patient Pharmaceutical Assessment Scheme: Citation Analysis, Document Review, Performance Metrics, and Media Perception Author

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author has previously provided medical advice to PHARMAC..
declarations.funderStatement: Nil.

detail.abstract:
Objective
Evaluate PHARMAC New Zealand's Named Patient Pharmaceutical Assessment (NPPA) using a convergent mixed-methods design integrating academic literature, institutional documents, performance metrics, and global media coverage.

Methods
Four studies were triangulated via O'Cathain's protocol: (1) citation scoping review (949 articles; six databases); (2) thematic analysis of PHARMAC annual reports (2016-2019) mapped to Donabedian's framework; (3) time-series analysis of NPPA metrics (2012-2024) using change-point detection and ARIMA; and (4) sentiment analysis and topic modelling of 1,133 media articles. Integration assessed convergence, complementarity, and divergence.

Results
NPPA showed operational efficiency with processing times of 17-21 days and an approval rate of 86.5%. Documents emphasised efficiency/timeliness and an increasing focus on transparency. Media coverage displayed a negativity bias: NPPA‑specific articles were more negative than general pharmaceutical policy coverage (−0.09 vs 0.17, p<0.001) despite high approval rates. Triangulation identified a “transparency paradox”: extensive process documentation alongside limited outcome evaluation and minimal scholarly attention.

Conclusions
NPPA is efficient and improvement‑oriented yet lacks systematic outcome reporting, creating accountability gaps. Addressing the transparency paradox requires routine, patient‑centred outcomes frameworks. Internationally, NPPA offers lessons in multi‑stage assessment, specialist committee use, and alignment with priority setting; remaining deficits mirror broader limitations of special‑access schemes. Mixed‑methods triangulation provided explanatory depth beyond single‑method designs.

title: Sharing Responsibilities along the AI Lifecycle: Towards a Responsible Labour AI Regulatory Regime

detail.title: Sharing Responsibilities along the AI Lifecycle: Towards a Responsible Labour AI Regulatory Regime

declarations.funderStatement: Israel Science Foundation

detail.abstract: The regulation of artificial intelligence (AI) systems in the workplace has emerged as a critical focus in the field of labour law. From a legal responsibilities perspective, much of the literature emphasizes the responsibilities of employers to safeguard employment rights and address work-related issues arising from the integration of these systems into the workplace. This emphasis includes ensuring that humans remain "in the loop" to oversee algorithmic processes and examining the role of unions in "negotiating the algorithm" with employers. Moreover, various countries and international organizations are enacting regulations that impose legal responsibilities on technology actors to uphold human rights, including specific labour rights and broader work-related concerns, such as algorithmic management. The main argument of this chapter is that without seriously considering the AI lifecycle in terms of work and the network of actors within this lifecycle, these two domains of legal responsibility-those governing employment relationships, whether individual or collectiveand those applied to technology actors of AI systems-are unable to promote a legal regime that takes labour consideration seriously. By closely examining the AI lifecycle and existing regulation at the EU level, the chapter proposes new directions of thought on how the regulation of employment relations and that of actors along the AI lifecycle can be interconnected and shared.

title: The Misuse of the Bayh-Dole Act and the Folly of Price Controls on Drug Patents
affiliations: George Mason University - Antonin Scalia Law School

detail.title: The Misuse of the Bayh-Dole Act and the Folly of Price Controls on Drug Patents

contentFormat.other: Forthcoming Chapter in "Bringing Medicines to Life: How Intellectual Property Enables Innovation in the Life Sciences" (eds. Jonathan M. Barnett and Bowman Heiden, Cambridge University Press, 2026)

detail.abstract: This chapter analyzes and critiques the “price control theory of the Bayh-Dole Act,” demonstrating that this decades-long campaign to use the Bayh-Dole Act to impose price controls on drug patents is both statutorily unjustified and policy folly. First, it provides novel statutory analyses of the Bayh-Dole Act to show once again that the text, structure, and function of the march-in power in § 203 precludes the National Institutes of Health (NIH) from using it to grant licenses to generic drug companies to reduce prices of prescription drugs. Second, it addresses the economic errors underlying this price-control agenda even when the NIH is legally authorized in other provisions of the Bayh-Dole Act to impose conditions on its grant agreements and licenses, such as price restrictions. Invoking this other statutory power in the Bayh-Dole Act, the Biden Administration adopted an “affordability” mandate in all licenses of NIH-owned patents in early 2025, and the Trump Administration officially implemented this policy on October 1, 2025. But this is policy folly. Contrary to conventional wisdom, almost all R&D funding for prescription drugs is from private sources. Given this economic data on drug R&D, a similar price-control policy adopted by the NIH in the early 1990s failed. In 1989, the NIH adopted a “reasonable pricing” condition in its research grant agreements and licenses for any resulting prescription drug. This policy resulted in a collapse of NIH research agreements and licenses. NIH Director Varmus thus withdrew the “reasonable pricing” mandate in 1995, expressly recognizing that it was contrary to the commercialization goals of the Bayh-Dole Act. The 2025 “affordability” mandate in NIH licenses will similarly commercialization of biomedical innovations. In sum, price controls on drug patents contravene the Bayh-Dole Act’s statutory text and function in harnessing the patent system as an engine of healthcare innovation through patent licensing and technology transfer.

title: Law, Political Economy, and Organizing for Tenant Power
affiliations: University of Pennsylvania Carey Law School

detail.title: Law, Political Economy, and Organizing for Tenant Power

declarations.declarationOfInterest: n/a
declarations.ethicsApproval: n/a
declarations.funderStatement: n/a

detail.abstract:
It is well acknowledged that the United States is facing a housing crisis, but the people who bare the brunt of this crisis, tenants of the multiracial working class, are often ignored in political and academic debates. Yet, tenants are organizing into tenant unions across the country to go on rent strike, to acquire their homes from neglectful landlords, and to pass bold tenant protection laws. This article 
seeks to give tenant organizing the attention it deserves as a solution to our perpetual housing crisis, and to encourage lawyers to join the tenant struggle in a supporting role.

title: The market for climate technologies

detail.title: The market for climate technologies
detail.abstract: This paper investigates the relationship between climate-related patent transactions and firm value, as measured by Tobin's Q. To conduct this analysis, I construct a novel firm-level panel dataset that combines patent transaction data, patent stock measures, and financial data. The results reveal that climate patent sales are associated with an immediate and persistent negative market reaction. However, climate patent acquisitions are linked to a delayed but positive market reaction that is evident one year after the transaction. Each additional climate patent sold per year is associated with a 2% decrease in firm value whereas each climate patent acquisition is associated with a 0.1% increase in firm value. These results survive a wide range of robustness checks that mitigate endogeneity concerns. By focusing on climate patent transactions rather than production, this study provides new evidence that markets penalize firms for divesting from potentially valuable climate technologies and partially reward firms that build technological options for future climate regulation. These findings highlight that climate patent transactions serve as credible signals of a firm's strategic orientation toward the climate transition.

title: Housing Crowding and Adolescent Educational Outcomes in China
affiliations: , University College London,  and University of Cambridge - Department of Land Economy

detail.title: Housing Crowding and Adolescent Educational Outcomes in China
detail.abstract: This paper investigates how childhood housing conditions shape long-term educational outcomes, with particular attention to gender disparities. Drawing on full-count microdata from the 2015 Chinese population census and historical housing exposure from 2010, we construct a county-level dataset to examine high school completion rates among adolescents aged 15-19—a critical transition beyond compulsory education. We find that improved housing conditions—such as larger per capita floor space and better access to basic facilities—are significantly associated with higher rates of high school completion. Our estimates are robust to controls and an instrumental variable (IV) model approach using housing conditions in neighboring counties. We further analyze longitudinal panel data from approximately 3,000 individuals in the China Family Panel Studies (CFPS), tracking their trajectories from adolescence (2010) to adulthood (2022). We show that adolescents who lived in crowded homes—defined as having less than 20 square meters of living space per capita—attain fewer years of schooling by adulthood. This negative effect is particularly pronounced among girls with male siblings in overcrowded households, who face up to 2.4 fewer years of schooling. This study extends the literature on environmental influences on educational outcomes and intergenerational mobility, by showing that not only neighborhood context, but also home-level housing conditions constitute a form of environmental inequality that shapes long-term educational trajectories.

title: Corruption and SDG 7: Affordable and Clean Energy
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Le Moyne College and IIT Madras, Department of Humanities and Social Sciences

detail.title: Corruption and SDG 7: Affordable and Clean Energy
detail.abstract: Over two billion people rely on traditional fuels for cooking, contributing to 3.5 million premature deaths annually, while the required $8 billion investment for a clean transition remains largely unmet. As of 2023, around 750 million people, primarily in Sub-Saharan Africa and Asia, still lack access to electricity, with projections suggesting that universal access (SDG 7.1.1) may not be achieved by 2030. Despite progress through renewable energy initiatives and proactive national policies, challenges remain, particularly in infrastructure, investment, and the persistent reliance on non-renewables. A critical, often underemphasized barrier is corruption, which undermines effective policy implementation and distorts public service delivery. Corruption pervades all levels; intermediaries, governments, and consumers weakening transparency, skewing resource allocation, and hampering international cooperation and technological innovation. Corruption not only inflates project costs by up to 50% but also stifles infrastructure expansion, innovation, and efficiency improvements. It weakens environmental regulation, facilitates rent-seeking in clean energy sectors, and deters foreign investment. Without strong anti-corruption frameworks, international cooperation, infrastructure development, and the promise of a sustainable energy future remain compromised. To achieve SDG 7, governance reform must be central-alongside financing, technology, and policy design-to ensure inclusive, efficient, and sustainable energy access.

title: Architectural Fairness: Eliminating Algorithmic Discrimination Through Population-of-One Calibration
affiliations: Epistria

detail.title: Architectural Fairness: Eliminating Algorithmic Discrimination Through Population-of-One Calibration
detail.abstract: This paper introduces Architectural Fairness, a population-of-one framework that makes algorithmic discrimination mathematically impossible by eliminating between-group variance. By achieving a 6–12× information-utilization advantage without demographic input, the Bias-Blind Behavioral Pattern Recognition Framework (BB-BPRF) transforms bias mitigation into a structural property with direct implications for liability, auditability, and insurance underwriting.

title: A DIALOGUE BETWEEN NON-COMPETE AND EARN-OUT CLAUSES IN M&A
affiliations: Pinheiro Neto Advogados, Universidade de Brasília (UnB) and

detail.title: A DIALOGUE BETWEEN NON-COMPETE AND EARN-OUT CLAUSES IN M&A
detail.abstract: The article examines the earn-out clause as a legal and financial mechanism designed to mitigate impasses arising from business valuation and to explore some of its competitive implications. It begins by analyzing the earn-out clause as a temporary solution for corporate valuation, outlining its main functions and structural models, and discussing its interpretation in post-closing disputes involving business contracts. The study then addresses the main competitive repercussions of earn-out clauses in business contracts, particularly their interaction with non-compete clauses and related issues under competition law. Finally, it offers didactic solutions, in table format, for the effective structuring of earn-out clauses, with the aim of enhancing their efficiency and mitigating possible conflicts, including antitrust concerns.

title: Does Formal Financial Development Crowd in Informal Financing? Evidence from Chinese Private Enterprises Highlights
affiliations: Xiamen University - School of Economics,  and Sichuan University - Business School

detail.title: Does Formal Financial Development Crowd in Informal Financing? Evidence from Chinese Private Enterprises Highlights
detail.abstract: The relationship between formal and informal finance is uncertain. They serve as substitute for high-quality borrowers but are complement for low-quality borrowers. As formal financial institutions expand, they may concentrate on high-quality borrowers or diversify among borrowers of different qualities. Using unique survey data from Chinese private firms, we are allowed to investigate the relationship for a group of borrowers who were considered as low-quality. We find that formal financial development imposes a crowd-in effect for private firms’ informal financing, especially in East China. There is heterogeneity between East and West China. We document that the crowd-in effect is greater for private firms with bank access or of large size.

title: SMALLHOLDER FARMERS' ADAPTATION TO RAINFALL VARIABILITY IN NORTHERN GHANA
affiliations: University for Development Studies, Faculty of Agribusiness and Communication Sciences, Students , University for Development Studies and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: SMALLHOLDER FARMERS' ADAPTATION TO RAINFALL VARIABILITY IN NORTHERN GHANA
detail.abstract: Irregular rainfall pattern pose challenges to smallholder farmers in Ghana, especially, those in the Northern Region, who risk losing their major source of livelihood as a result of the devastating impacts of climate change. To ensure food and livelihood security, smallholder farmers adopt indigenous and modern soil and water conservation strategies. This study therefore examined the influencing factors of adaptation to irregular rainfall pattern and the challenges therein. A cross sectional data of 140 households from five (5) randomly selected districts in the Northern region of Ghana was used. Results of a Negative Binomial Regression showed that access to extension services and credit positively influenced the number of adaptation strategies to irregular rainfall pattern. Also, quantity harvested, gender and age negatively influenced the number of adaptation strategies adopted by a farmer. Consistently, lack of credit was the first major constraint to climate adaptation among the farmers. The

title: Carrot and Stick: Impact of Regulations, Subsidies, and Obligations on the Development of Cashless Payments in Poland 105
affiliations: Nicolaus Copernicus University, Nicolaus Copernicus University in Toruń, University of Warsaw - Faculty of Management, Vrije Universiteit Brussel (VUB) - Applied Economics Department, Nicolas Copernicus University in Torun, Nicolaus Copernicus University and Nicolaus Copernicus University

detail.title: Carrot and Stick: Impact of Regulations, Subsidies, and Obligations on the Development of Cashless Payments in Poland 105
detail.abstract: Between 2012 and 2024, Poland—once a laggard in cash- less payments among EU countries—underwent a profound trans- formation. The per capita number of cashless transactions at physical points of sale increased more than eightfold, rising from approximately 30 to over 250 per year, surpassing the EU average. While the number of payment cards per capita grew by about 40%, payment terminals per one million inhabitants increased almost fivefold, from 7,500 to 36,700. This paper adopts a two-stage analytical approach to examine whether policies introduced over the past decade influenced the growth in payment terminals and cards, and ultimately, the volume of cashless transactions. These policies include regulations of the interchange fee level, a program to subsidize payment terminals for merchants, and the introduction of the legal ob- ligation for merchants to accept cashless instruments. Our findings indicate that the first two policies—interchange fee regulation and terminal subsidies—positively affected the expansion of the acceptance network. In turn, this expansion had a statistically significant impact on the growth of cashless payment usage.

title: New Technologies and Globalization in Public Administration

detail.abstract: This research explored the dynamic interaction between emerging technologies and globalization within the field of public administration. In an era characterized by rapid technological progress and an increasingly interconnected global landscape, public administrations worldwide face new challenges and opportunities. This study delves into the multifaceted impacts of emerging technologies on the theory and practice of public administration within the context of globalization. The research took a comprehensive, interdisciplinary approach, drawing insights from various fields, including political science, economics, sociology, and information technology. It investigated how modern technologies like artificial intelligence, big data analytics, blockchain, and e-governance solutions were restructuring the operations and effectiveness of public administration at local, national, and international levels. Additionally, the study explored how globalization both fuels and responds to these technological changes.

title: Active Disruption: A Meta-Theory of Corporate Survival in the Age of AI

detail.title: Active Disruption: A Meta-Theory of Corporate Survival in the Age of AI

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.ethicsApproval: None
declarations.funderStatement: None

detail.abstract: This paper proposes "Active Disruption Theory," a new management paradigm for the era of technological homogenization driven by Artificial Intelligence (AI). We argue that as AI transforms traditional technological and efficiency advantages into commoditized infrastructure (McKinsey, 2025), the only definitive competitive moat for a firm becomes its intrinsic philosophy and "world model." This theory challenges the traditional management paradigm centered on "building and controlling," advocating instead for the disciplined, proactive self-dismantling of "vested interests" to resolve "form tension," thereby shaping the organization into an "antifragile" system that continuously benefits from nonlinear shocks (Taleb, 2012). Through a comparative case study of Kodak, Sony, and Alibaba, we illustrate the divergent outcomes of "mending to evade" versus "dismantling to prepare." The theory provides a new actionable framework for managers, shifting from "avoiding failure" to "profiting from failure," and extends the literature on dynamic capabilities to offer an operational theory for organizational survival and evolution under uncertainty.

title: APPLICATION OF DATA SECURITY IN ORGANIZATIONS WITH REFERENCE TO BANGALORE
affiliations: and Velalar College of Engineering and Technology

detail.title: APPLICATION OF DATA SECURITY IN ORGANIZATIONS WITH REFERENCE TO BANGALORE
detail.abstract: This paper presents the application of data security in organizations, emphasizing its significance in the digital age. The introduction establishes data as a core organizational asset, in danger to various threats. To address these vulnerabilities, the methodology section outlines a comprehensive framework encompassing Access Controls, Data Encryption, Data Loss Prevention (DLP), Employee Training, Backup and Recovery, Security Software. Results section is envisioned to present the findings from implementing above outlined methodologies and the discussion section would then analyse these results, exploring the impact of the implemented data security measures. It would delve into the effectiveness of the chosen methodology in achieving its objectives, identify potential areas for improvement, and discuss the broader implications for organizational data security practices. Findings section includes metrics demonstrating reduced security incidents, improved data access, control effectiveness, or enhanced employee awareness of data security practices. In conclusion, this paper aims to provide a comprehensive overview of data security application in organizations. By presenting a multifaceted methodology, analysing its results, and fostering discussion, this work intends to contribute valuable insights to the ongoing pursuit of robust data protection within organizations.

title: Coordinated Monetary and Fiscal Framework for Debt Management

detail.title: Coordinated Monetary and Fiscal Framework for Debt Management
detail.abstract: This paper outlines a proposal for a coordinated macroeconomic policy framework aimed at achieving long-term debt sustainability while promoting maximum employment and stable inflation. The strategy involves a rule-based Open Market Operations (OMO) policy for the central bank, combined with a benchmarked fiscal taxation policy with automatic adjustments. This framework seeks to address the limitations of relying solely on either monetary or fiscal policy, enhance predictability, and maintain central bank independence within a defined structure. Drawing upon established economic concepts such as fiscal rules, and the importance of central bank credibility, this paper presents a practical and systematic approach for policymakers. This approach aims to stimulate the economy during weak and normal phases while ensuring that excess liquidity is later harvested through targeted taxation and debt reduction once growth materializes. This framework prevents overburdening strained economies with new taxes while enhancing fiscal sustainability.

title: Motivated memory and favoritism *
affiliations: Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (LMU)

detail.title: Motivated memory and favoritism *
detail.abstract: Many important decisions that involve the judgement of others are based on recalled information. Such reliance on memory may interact with favoritism-a pervasive source of inefficiency and inequality in organizations. This paper investigates how reliance on memory amplifies favoritism in personnel decisions. In an online experiment, managers make incentivized hiring decisions regarding workers of varying quality. Two experimental manipulations isolate the causal effect of memory on favoritism. First, I experimentally vary managers' preferences for workers. Second, I vary between-subjects whether managers base their choices on workers' quality or on their recall of that quality. I find that when decisions rely on memory, the gap in the hiring probability between favored and non-favored workers more than doubles from 10 to 21 percentage points. Turning to the mechanisms, I find that motivated memories drive around one third of this effect: managers remember favored workers as being of higher quality than unfavored ones.

detail.abstract: This paper develops a formal theory of discrimination as a profit-oriented economic activity, in which agents allocate time and resources to exclude competitors in pursuit of private gains. The model introduces time constraints, punishment risk, and market equilibrium to determine the endogenous discrimination rate. We show that policy instruments-taxation of discriminatory profits, sanctions, institutional strengthening, and support to discriminated groups-reduce aggregate exposure e * through distinct channels. The framework also predicts that offender density generates congestion effects, weakening enforcement outcomes. Finally, we discuss extensions on agent heterogeneity, human capital, and the role of the public sector, offering a bridge between theory, empirical evidence, and public policy.

title: Reflexivity in Financial Markets: A Theoretical Framework Extending the Black-Scholes Model

detail.title: Reflexivity in Financial Markets: A Theoretical Framework Extending the Black-Scholes Model
detail.abstract: Extensive research has been conducted on the creation of models to predict market movement, with the Black-Scholes model being a cornerstone. The Black-Scholes model has been an integral part of modern financial theory, providing a mathematical framework for option prices under the assumption of exogenous market dynamics. However, in practice, financial markets are reflexive: Trading strategies based on mathematical models take as input the very variables that were affected by investing using these models. This challenges the core assumption of market efficiency in traditional financial theory. This research proposes a framework to formally introduce reflexivity into the Black-Scholes model. Specifically, we explore three mechanisms through which reflexivity alters market dynamics: (i) predictability of Brownian motion when trader dependence on mathematical model introduces path dependence, (ii) deviation of the drift coefficient from risk-free rate in a risk-neutral world due to large-scale institutional model use, and (iii) endogeneity of volatility. By reformulating the stochastic differential equation for asset price to include the above reflexivity-induced changes, we can show how reflexivity fundamentally alters option pricing dynamics. This framework advances the literature on market reflexivity, originally popularized by George Soros, by providing a formal mathematical structure linked to option pricing theory. The paper offers a pathway to rethink volatility estimation, systemic risk amplification, and the limits of using mathematical models in the financial market under the assumption that inputs are exogenous. This paper highlights the need for paradigm shift: the market cannot be assumed exogenous when the widespread use of mathematical models for investments actively shapes the inputs that are fed into the same models.

title: Assessment of Critical Gap at Uncontrolled Intersections Under Mixed Traffic Conditions: A Review
affiliations: and National Institute of technology srinagar

detail.title: Assessment of Critical Gap at Uncontrolled Intersections Under Mixed Traffic Conditions: A Review
detail.abstract: Critical gap analysis is essential in finding capacity, sight distance, queue length, and delay at uncontrolled intersections. Maximum studies on critical gap estimation have been conducted in developed countries, where traffic is homogenous and lane disciplines and priority rules have been followed. However, in India, like many other developing countries traffic is heterogenous and priority rules are not followed thoroughly which consequently leads to conflicts at intersections thus modeling such behavior becomes complex. In developing countries like India, traffic is heterogeneous, and priority rules are less respected, leading to conflicts at intersections, and modeling such behavior becomes complex. This paper reviews research conducted on the gap acceptance behavior of drivers at uncontrolled intersections. It presents and discusses work done concerning different critical gap analysis techniques. It discusses the merits/demerits of using various gap acceptance methods developed for homogeneous traffic conditions and those devised for mixed traffic conditions. Two 3-legged unsignalized junctions were chosen in a peri-urban landscape of Srinagar city in the union territory of Jammu and Kashmir, India, in contemplation of finding gap acceptance behavior of drivers in case of mixed traffic scenario. Various road surveys and videography had been conducted to collect the data. This research utilizes fifteen existing techniques to estimate the critical gap values for the left turn, through or straight, and right turn maneuver of four different categories of vehicles. In this paper, a comparison of different approaches of critical gap estimation is performed and addresses their condemnatory investigation. The range of critical gap values, their reliability, and the procedures followed in different countries is critically analyzed in this article. Most of the procedures do not portray an accurate picture of the critical gap under mixed traffic conditions. However, the occupancy time method, absolute difference method, and clearing behavior approach show significant results since these techniques utilize heterogeneous traffic conditions. At the end of this article, the technique that suits the most for assessing the critical gap values in case of heterogeneous traffic conditions is presented.

reference: European Corporate Governance Institute – Finance Working Paper Forthcoming
title: Politics and Finance
affiliations: , Indiana University - Kelley School of Business - Department of Finance and Pennsylvania State University - Department of Finance

detail.title: Politics and Finance

publicationDetails.detailsText: European Corporate Governance Institute – Finance Working Paper Forthcoming
publicationDetails.journalName: European Corporate Governance Institute (ECGI) - Finance Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: Rising government intervention, corporate political spending, and geopolitical rifts underscore the importance of the link between politics and finance. This review describes how politics affects firms, banks, households, and markets. Companies form political ties through board connections, lobbying, revolving-door hires, and contributions. In return, they gain access to procurement contracts, cheaper debt, bailouts, policy information, and reduced enforcement. Political ties are generally associated with increased shareholder value but can also be costly during periods of political disruption. Political factors spill over to banking, where banks favor connected firms and secure regulatory forbearance; to households, whose partisan beliefs shape investments; to asset markets, which price political risk; and to global capital markets, where investment and banking flows respond to geopolitical risks. We conclude with open questions, including which types of money matter most in politics, how politics influences relational contracts, and the need to integrate political economy factors into finance theory.

title: Drivers of New Business Creation in the OECD: The Role of Education and Taxation
affiliations: ISEG Lisbon School of Economics and Management,Universidade de Lisboa, University of Malaga and Universidad de Málaga

detail.title: Drivers of New Business Creation in the OECD: The Role of Education and Taxation
detail.abstract: The main aim of this paper is to empirically assess the impact of education and tax revenue on fostering new business creation in the OECD countries. To this end, we employ fixed effects and random effects models using panel data from 2006 to 2022, incorporating alternative conditions. Results confirm that while education and the economic situation are key pillars in fostering new business creation, the role of tax revenue in supporting economic development – and, by extension, new business formation – is fundamental, even if non-linear, with a threshold of 30% of GDP. Tax revenue collected by governments provides essential funding for public goods and services such as infrastructure, education, and innovation support programs, all of which contribute to creating an environment where new businesses can emerge and thrive. Our findings remain robust under the GMM estimation.

title: Assisted Governance with LLM-based Algorithmic Committees: Reliability, Systematic Divergence, and a Tiered-Trust Workflow
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Assisted Governance with LLM-based Algorithmic Committees: Reliability, Systematic Divergence, and a Tiered-Trust Workflow
detail.abstract: Effective organizational governance hinges on collective intelligence, yet human groups are susceptible to biases and narrow perspectives. Can AI improve this process? We conceptualize LLMs as programmable governance participants that introduce cognitive diversity, and we construct LLM-based algorithmic committees—programmable ensembles of evaluator personas , explicit aggregation rules, and human oversight.Our research is grounded in a dataset we curated of 508 real proposals from Nouns DAO, enriched with dynamic financial and market context from the time of their submission. We then deployed LLM-based algorithmic committees to conduct a large-scale evaluation, generating a primary corpus of 21,336 structured judgments for analysis and auditing its reliability with a separate 16,618 re-run experiment. Three results stand out. First, behavior is instruction-dominant, demonstrating a practical lever for programmable cognitive diversity. Second, committee recommendations systematically diverge from historical human choices, surfacing value-explicit counter-perspectives rather than imitation. Third, reliability splits across outputs: final votes are sensitive to sampling parameters, whereas multi-criteria scores—and especially textual reasons—are robust. These findings extend collective-intelligence theory to human-AI assemblages and motivate a Tiered-Trust workflow: expose/audit reasons, use scores diagnostically, and treat votes cautiously with uncertainty gates that escalate to humans. This practical framework is designed for broad application in any organization engaging in complex decision-making, from DAOs to traditional review boards and compliance committees."

title: Inequality and Market Power: Evidence from the United States and China
affiliations: , University of Milan and INSE at Peking University

detail.title: Inequality and Market Power: Evidence from the United States and China
detail.abstract: Using barcode-level data from the NielsenIQ Homescan Consumer Panel, we study how income inequality affects the prices of identical goods across US counties. We find that higher inequality reduces prices for products with low market shares but increases prices for products with high market shares. With higher inequality, larger firms, which sell more high-market-share goods, tend to raise prices, while smaller firms lower them. We find a similar pattern using Chinese export data across countries. To interpret these findings, we develop a model where a mean-preserving spread in income affects pricing through the convexity of demand and the convexity of the price derivative of demand with respect to income. We derive conditions under which inequality raises the price elasticity for low-market-share products and lowers it for high-market-share products, matching our empirical results.

title: Do Models Matter? How Parent, Offspring, and Sibling Relationships Shape the Diffusion of AI Innovations
affiliations: Case Western Reserve University - Weatherhead School of Management

detail.title: Do Models Matter? How Parent, Offspring, and Sibling Relationships Shape the Diffusion of AI Innovations
detail.abstract: Artificial Intelligence has spread rapidly across research and practice, yet we know little about how AI knowledge diffuses through the models that embody it. This study examines how relationships among AI models—those they build on (parents), those derived from them (offspring), and those developed in parallel (siblings)—influence the diffusion of AI research. We combine data from Papers with Code, OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, and GitHub, covering over sixty-four thousand papers and nearly one hundred thousand models from 2000 to 2023. Using a heterogeneous temporal graph neural network, CITE-Net, and econometric analysis, we find that papers linked to focal models with moderate centrality gain the most attention, offspring models show a U-shaped effect where renewed adoption boosts visibility, and parent models exhibit a steady negative effect as reliance on older models fades. These results reveal how evolving model genealogies shape the spread of AI innovations across research communities.

title: CALL FOR DEBT RELEASE FOR SUSTAINABLE HUMAN DEVELOPMENT: A Jubilee Initiative for a Generative Cooperation Between Creditors and Debtors
affiliations: University of Rome Tor Vergata - Faculty of Economics, University of Tuscia, University of Milan, affiliation not provided to SSRN and University of Pavia - Università degli Studi di Pavia

detail.title: CALL FOR DEBT RELEASE FOR SUSTAINABLE HUMAN DEVELOPMENT: A Jubilee Initiative for a Generative Cooperation Between Creditors and Debtors

contentType.other: A detailed and sound illustration of the debt release initiative

contentFormat.other: A call for a debt release initiative

detail.abstract: The debt degeneration and the cycles of debt unsustainability are one of the systemic issues that cause and fuel economic and social injustices around the world. Moreover, the Catholic Church, has also increasingly emphasized the concept of ecological debt as a critical dimension of global justice. This ecological debt arises not only from greenhouse gas emissions, which have historically been dominated by the industrialized countries which have created the largest part of the global warming problem, but also from environmental degradation linked to extractive industries, toxic waste exports, and lax environmental regulations in poorer nations. The result is a double burden on the Global South: environmental degradation coupled with limited economic capacity to invest in sustainable development. This moral insight offers a prophetic foundation for an actionable debt strategy for sustainable human development. This comprehensive strategy aims to cancel part of a developing country's foreign debt in exchange for commitments to invest in local projects on environmental conservation, renewable energy to mitigate emissions, or climate adaptation, according to the UN framework of Sustainable Development Goals. According to the UN approach and ESG criteria, the generative cooperation between creditors and debtors will take the form of a guarantee & development fund fed by debt service that creditors renounce to earn with a democratic governance thanks to the participation of international, national and local civil society. In order to "leave no one behind" (Pope Francis, World Food Day 2023), this debt release strategy aims to provide economic and political support to "forgive the debts of countries that will never be able to repay them" (Pope Francis, Spes non confundit, 2025) by starting to promote the financial and institutional leverage of Special Drawing Rights, accumulated by high-income countries thanks to the IMF allocation in 2021.

title: Learning to Price under Competition with Reference Price Effects
affiliations: Wuhan University, Wuhan University and

detail.title: Learning to Price under Competition with Reference Price Effects
detail.abstract: This paper addresses the algorithmic design of price competition in oligopolistic markets, with a focus on long-run market dynamics under reference price effects. We consider a sequential price competition framework with multiple sellers operating over a finite horizon, each lacking prior knowledge of the demand functions. Consumer demand depends not only on current prices but also on a reference price, defined as a weighted average of past prices that shape consumer expectations. We characterize market stability through the concept of a Stationary Nash Equilibrium (SNE), where no seller has an incentive to deviate unilaterally and the reference price remains stable. To operate under incomplete demand information and limited observability of competitors' prices, we propose a Simultaneous Perturbation Stochastic Approximation with Callbacks (SPSAC) policy. Despite the lack of a monotonicity condition, which is typically required for convergence in online games, we show that this policy achieves a last-iterate convergence rate of $\mathcal{O}(1/\sqrt{T})$ for joint prices and reference prices toward the SNE, along with a dynamic regret of $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{T})$. We further consider two extensions. First, when sellers have access to first-order feedback, the convergence rate improves to $\mathcal{O}(1/T)$, highlighting the value of demand information in simplifying sequential price competition. Second, when prices have long-term effects on the reference price, causing demand to evolve as a non-stationary stochastic process, our policy still guarantees $\mathcal{O}(1/\sqrt{T})$ convergence and $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{T})$ dynamic regret.

title: Role of Global Oil Market Shocks on Macroeconomic Variables: An SVAR Approach to the Nigerian Economy
affiliations: Nigerian Economic Summit Group and Obafemi Awolowo University

detail.title: Role of Global Oil Market Shocks on Macroeconomic Variables: An SVAR Approach to the Nigerian Economy
detail.abstract: This study examines the effects of structural shocks in the global oil market on Nigeria's key macroeconomic variables. Recognising that oil price movements reflect diverse underlying forces, the analysis distinguishes between oil supply shocks, aggregate demand shocks, and oil-specific demand shocks. Using a Structural Vector Autoregressive (SVAR) framework following Kilian (2009), the study traces how each category of global oil shock transmits to Nigeria's exchange rate and economic activity. The methodology incorporates Augmented Dickey-Fuller, Phillips-Perron, and Zivot-Andrews unit root tests, alongside Johansen, Gregory-Hansen, and Hatemi-J cointegration procedures to account for potential structural breaks in the data. Dynamic responses are assessed using impulse response functions and variance decompositions. The empirical results indicate that variations in oil prices are primarily driven by global real economic activity and oil-specific demand shocks, while supply-side disruptions exert minimal influence. Both global demand and oil-specific shocks significantly affect Nigeria's exchange rate and economic activity, but no long-run cointegration is found among the variables. The analysis further reveals the absence of a meaningful pass-through between the exchange rate and domestic output. These findings underscore Nigeria's continued vulnerability to external oil market dynamics and the limited effectiveness of exchange rate policy as a stabilising tool. The study concludes that policy efforts should prioritise structural diversification and productivity-enhancing reforms to reduce exposure to oil market volatility and strengthen macroeconomic resilience.

title: The Real and Financial Effects of Local Corporate Tax Increases: Evidence from Linked Firm–Bank Data
affiliations: NOVA SBE Health Economics & Management Knowledge Center and

detail.title: The Real and Financial Effects of Local Corporate Tax Increases: Evidence from Linked Firm–Bank Data
detail.abstract: We study how local corporate tax increases affect firms’ financing and real activity. In Portugal, municipalities independently set a surtax on corporate income, generating plausibly exogenous variation across space and time. We link the universe of corporate balance sheets and profit-and-loss statements to loan-level data from the Bank of Portugal’s credit registry, allowing us to track firms’ liquidity, leverage, borrowing costs, and credit quality alongside revenues, inputs, employment, and productivity. We estimate local-projection difference-in-differences models that address staggered treatment timing and dynamic responses. Surtax hikes immediately tighten financing conditions: liquidity falls, implicit interest rates rise, debt increases at shorter maturities, and non-performing loans become more prevalent. These strains spill over into real outcomes: firms reduce sales, inputs, and employment and experience persistent declines in total factor productivity. Effects are strongest among small and young firms, where leverage rises in response to liquidity losses, while larger firms increase leverage in line with tax-shield incentives. We also find higher exit and relocation probabilities, but no gains in neighboring output, pointing to inefficient reallocation. Our results highlight how local tax policy can transmit through both financial and real margins, with implications for fiscal design in decentralized settings.

title: Africa Fighting an Unofficial Economic War to Govern Itself
affiliations: Durban University of Technology, Durban University of Technology, University of South Africa (UNISA) and University of South Africa (UNISA)

detail.title: Africa Fighting an Unofficial Economic War to Govern Itself
detail.abstract: This paper analyses Africa's pursuit of economic sovereignty in the context of external influences and internal conflicts, particularly focusing on the impact of multinational corporations. It utilizes case studies from 30 articles between 2003 and 2025 to illustrate the effects of resource extraction and trade agreements on local economies, contrasting expected benefits with actual outcomes. The research highlights governance issues and socio-economic inequality while advocating for regional integration and local entrepreneurship as means for enhancing self-governance and resilience, aiming for a more autonomous economic future in Africa

title: A New Quantitative Credit Rating Criteria
affiliations: NYU/Courant

detail.title: A New Quantitative Credit Rating Criteria
detail.abstract: Credit rating changes are bound to happen, simply because both fundamentals and market conditions change during the life of ratings. Excessive changes are not welcomed, however, by almost all stakeholders, including issuers, investors, and regulators, as exemplified by the wave of massive rating downgrades during the great financial crisis of 2007-2009. Mitigating rating volatility has since become an urgent public demand. While significant efforts in straightening the quantitative and non-quantitative aspects of the credit rating process have been made, the fundamental issue of rating cyclicality has not been adequately addressed, as the quantitative rating measures of credit risk have remained the same cyclical ones, either probability of default or the expected loss. This article introduces a new credit rating criteria by synthesizing the expected loss with unexpected loss or economic capital. It is hoped that the acyclical economic capital measure allows credit ratings to better respond in an acyclical manner. Rating change simulation based on Merton model with a mean-reverting stochastic volatility model shows significant reduction in numbers of rating changes for the band of AA-/Aa3 to B-/B3 ratings.

title: Project Management Strategies in Smart Transportation Networks: Challenges and Opportunities in Developing Countries
affiliations: Oxford Academy and George Mason University

detail.title: Project Management Strategies in Smart Transportation Networks: Challenges and Opportunities in Developing Countries
detail.abstract: The evolution of transportation systems toward digitalisation and intelligent automation has transformed global mobility. However, in developing countries, the integration of Smart Transportation Networks (STNs) remains hindered by infrastructural limitations, governance gaps, and resource constraints. This study explores the project management strategies essential for the successful planning, implementation, and sustainability of smart transportation initiatives within such contexts. Using a qualitative narrative-synthesis methodology, the research analyses case studies, academic literature, and institutional frameworks from 2015 to 2025 to identify patterns, challenges, and best practices in the management of technology-enabled transportation projects. The study's central contribution is the development of a Strategic Project Management Framework for Smart Transportation (SPMF-ST)-a model integrating project governance, stakeholder coordination, risk mitigation, and technology alignment for developing economies. Findings reveal that successful smart transportation initiatives depend on adaptive project management practices combining traditional methods with agile and systems-thinking approaches. Key determinants of success include strong institutional leadership, stakeholder collaboration, data-driven decision-making, and continuous capacity building. Conversely, barriers such as fragmented governance, insufficient funding, and limited technical expertise impede progress. The research concludes that the future of smart mobility in developing countries depends not only on technology investment but also on strategic project management competence. The proposed framework offers policymakers and project leaders a roadmap for implementing sustainable, scalable, and contextually adapted smart transportation systems that align with UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs 9, 11, and 13)industry innovation, sustainable cities, and climate action.

title: INTEGRATION OF ANCIENT INDIAN CLASSICAL TEXTS IN CONTEMPORARY BANKING PRACTICES
affiliations: Guru Ghasidas Vishwavidyalaya - Department of Commerce

detail.title: INTEGRATION OF ANCIENT INDIAN CLASSICAL TEXTS IN CONTEMPORARY BANKING PRACTICES
detail.abstract: This paper investigates the significance of ancient Indian classical texts in modern banking. By studying ancient Indian texts such as the Arthashastra, Manusmriti, Yajnavalkyasmriti, and Vedas, as well as historical records and inscriptions from the Mauryan and Gupta periods. The paper investigates the principles and practices of banking and finance in ancient India. The paper argues that many of the concepts and ideas presented in these texts are still relevant today and can provide valuable insights for the modern banking business. Examples include the importance of ethical conduct, risk management, and the use of financial instruments such as hundis. The paper suggests that modern banks can improve their practises and better serve the needs of society by drawing on the wisdom of these ancient texts. Overall, the paper contributes to a better understanding of the intersection of ancient Indian wisdom and modern banking business practises.

reference: Abhay Shukla, Research Scholar, UPRTOU Prayagraj
title: A Multi-Stage Approach to Government-Citizen Dialogue in the ACACAE Model: The Government-Citizen Interactive Communication

detail.title: A Multi-Stage Approach to Government-Citizen Dialogue in the ACACAE Model: The Government-Citizen Interactive Communication

declarations.ethicsApproval: This study did not involve human participants, patients, or personally identifiable data. Therefore, formal ethics approval was not required, as per institutional and research ethics guidelines. The research relied solely on secondary data sources, including academic publications, policy documents, and official e-governance frameworks. All sources have been appropriately cited to maintain academic integrity and transparency.

publicationDetails.detailsText: Abhay Shukla, Research Scholar, UPRTOU Prayagraj

detail.abstract: This research introduces the ACACAE Model, a six-step process that conceptualizes government-citizen discourse as a dynamic and cyclical process of communication between Awareness, Communication/Consultation, Adoption, Collaboration, Advocacy, and Empowerment. Different from conventional e-governance models that emphasize mere efficiency, the ACACAE model focuses on participatory governance based on trust, participation, and constant feedback. The model reframes digital governance as an interactive and co-creative system wherein each step cumulatively adds to the next to ensure authentic citizen empowerment. In order to close the gap between abstract theory and quantifiable practice, the study presents the Government-Citizen Communication Effectiveness Index (GC-Index), a mathematical construct that measures participation from 0 (zero dialogue) to 1 (full empowerment). The GC-Index combines additive stage development with multiplicative systemic modifiers-Trust (T), Inclusivity (I), Feedback (F), and Barriers (B)-so that institutional coherence has a direct impact on the quality of exchange. Employing a qualitative approach, the paper illustrates that genuine democratic legitimacy stems not from technology uptake but from continuous cycles of trust-based communication. The ACACAE-GC model, therefore provides policymakers with a diagnostic tool to assess dialogue effectiveness, enhance accountability, and promote participatory governance.

title: The Collapse of Academic Freedom: How Institutional Gatekeeping has Silenced Scientific Discourse
affiliations: Shenyang Normal University

detail.title: The Collapse of Academic Freedom: How Institutional Gatekeeping has Silenced Scientific Discourse
detail.abstract: This article examines the erosion of academic freedom in contemporary scholarly publishing, revealing how institutional gatekeeping and subjective editorial standards have replaced open intellectual competition. Once a realm where logically argued viewpoints could be published regardless of mainstream acceptance, academia now systematically excludes ideas that threaten established paradigms or authority. Through analysis of editorial rejection practices and peer review bias, the article details how technical correctness is subordinated to judgments of "importance," resulting in the suppression of theoretical innovation and error correction. The article calls for deep reform: restoring transparent, merit-based evaluation and embracing open competition as the path to true scientific progress.

title: The EU Anti-Money Laundering Authority: A Strategic Roadmap
affiliations: University of Malta - Department of Banking and Finance

detail.title: The EU Anti-Money Laundering Authority: A Strategic Roadmap
detail.abstract: Financial crises often trigger pivotal changes in regulatory frameworks, fostering the establishment of specialised agencies to address emerging policy challenges. The recent formation of the EU Anti-Money-Laundering Authority (AMLA) marks a significant advancement in the European Union’s efforts to combat money laundering and the financing of terrorism (AML/CFT). Established as part of the European Commission’s 2021 initiative, AMLA is tasked with enhancing the identification of suspicious financial activities, fortifying oversight of high-risk cross-border financial entities and improving nonfinancial sector supervision through collaborative assessments. This paper contends that AMLA’s immediate priorities should encompass the structuring of governance and infrastructure, the enhancement of operational capacity, the adoption of a balanced regulatory framework and proactive stakeholder engagement. It emphasises the necessity for AMLA to align its efforts with recent recommendations aimed at bolstering Europe’s competitiveness while effectively addressing financial crime. By leveraging the experiences of existing European Supervisory Authorities, such as the European Securities and Markets Authority, AMLA can facilitate a cohesive regulatory environment and achieve supervisory consistency. These insights were derived from discussions presented by the author during a panel at the EUROFI forum in Budapest in September 2024, outlining key strategies for AMLA’s successful implementation amidst complex regulatory challenges. This article is included in The Business and Management Collection (https://hstalks.com/business/).

title: Systemic Issues in Microwave Absorption Research
affiliations: Shenyang Normal University

detail.title: Systemic Issues in Microwave Absorption Research
detail.abstract: This commentary examines the systemic failures underlying contemporary research on microwave absorption, revealing how flawed theoretical frameworks have become entrenched through institutional inertia, editorial bias, and the misuse of citation metrics. Despite numerous high-impact publications in Advanced Materials, Advanced Functional Materials, Nature Communications, and PNAS, most studies continue to rely on the traditional impedance-matching and quarter-wavelength theories-models that conflate film and bulk behaviors and contradict the principles of wave interference.

title: Leadership in Institution of Higher Learning and Host Community: A Qualitative Analysis of Dennis Osadebay University and Ben Oghojafor-Asaba Relations
affiliations: Dennis Osadebay University

detail.title: Leadership in Institution of Higher Learning and Host Community: A Qualitative Analysis of Dennis Osadebay University and Ben Oghojafor-Asaba Relations
detail.abstract: This paper interrogates Professor Ben Oghojafor's leadership at Dennis Osadebay University with a specific focus on Oghojafor's relationship with Asaba the host community. While the study uses qualitative method for data analysis it employs secondary sources mainly books, journal articles, and newspapers for data collection. The findings of the study indicate that Ben Oghojafor-Asaba relations was triggered by the wider and open-minded acceptance of the establishment of Dennis Osadebay University by Asaba community that viewed the University project as a welcome development having yearned for the creation of the institution for many years. Oghojafor, eager to make history as the first Vice Chancellor of the institution have continued to work towards maintaining peaceful coexistence between the University and Asaba community though with some pockets of challenges that is obtainable in other institutions of higher learning and their host communities. The implication is that as a university that started from the scratch, instead of attracting relevant oppositions to issues, maximum and mutual support is needed from the host community for the growth of Dennis Osadebay University in the overall interests of all.
