detail.abstract:
This volume inaugurates the Alaali Financial Models Meta-Framework (AFMF), a doctrinal structure uniting behavioral finance, sustainability, and ethical intelligence under the Dynamic Financial Applied Science (DFAS) continuum. The opening model, AFMF-SFBM-F01 — The Alaali Self-Funded Behavioral Control Model (A-SFBM) establishes a self-regenerative behavioral–financial mechanism where operational efficiency finances its own incentives. By redefining control as a self-funding behavioral cycle, the model bridges financial rationality, human motivation, and operational discipline, founding the new field of Behavioral Managerial Finance (BMF).
This volume includes twelve doctrinal manuscripts tracing the evolution from behavioral efficiency to ethical intelligence and provides the first integrated theory of self-funded behavioral governance in finance.

title: DOES THE SUPREME COURT OF NIGERIA HAVE JURISDICTION TO HEAR APPEALS THAT ARE BASED ON MIXED LAW AND FACTS?
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: DOES THE SUPREME COURT OF NIGERIA HAVE JURISDICTION TO HEAR APPEALS THAT ARE BASED ON MIXED LAW AND FACTS?
detail.abstract: This paper examines whether the Supreme Court of Nigeria retains jurisdiction to hear appeals based on mixed law and facts following the enactment of the Constitution (Second Alteration) Act, 2010. The research highlights that prior to the amendment, the Supreme Court could entertain appeals both as of right and with leave under Section 233 of the 1999 Constitution. However, Section 6 of the Second Alteration Act replaced the entire provision, effectively removing the Court's power to hear appeals with leave. Through an analysis of recent judicial decisions, particularly Shittu v. PAN Ltd., Amadi v. Wopara, and Anyanwu v. Emmanuel, the paper demonstrates the evolution and eventual clarification of this jurisdictional issue. It concludes that the concurring judgment of Salauwa, J.S.C., in Anyanwu v. Emmanuel conclusively affirms that the Supreme Court no longer has jurisdiction to hear appeals on mixed law and facts, thereby reinforcing its role as a court of law rather than a forum for factual re-evaluation.

title: The Mediating Role of Administrative Empowerment in the Relationship Between Ethical Leadership and Job Performance in Public Joint-Stock Companies
affiliations: Sana'a University, Thamar University and Amran Universtiy

detail.title: The Mediating Role of Administrative Empowerment in the Relationship Between Ethical Leadership and Job Performance in Public Joint-Stock Companies
detail.abstract: This study aims to investigate the mediating role of administrative empowerment in the relationship between ethical leadership and job performance within Yemeni public joint-stock companies, which play a vital role in supporting the national economy. Employing a descriptive quantitative approach, the research utilized Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) to analyze data from 433 employees across eight companies. The measurement model demonstrated strong psychometric properties, with outer loadings ≥ 0.70, composite reliability ≥ 0.86, and Average Variance Extracted (AVE) ≥ 0.56. The structural model revealed a significant impact of ethical leadership on administrative empowerment (β = 0.83) and of administrative empowerment on job performance (β = 0.86), while no direct effect was found between ethical leadership and job performance (β = 0.070). However, administrative empowerment showed a strong mediating effect (β = 0.717), explaining 69% of the variance in administrative empowerment and 85% in job performance, indicating high predictive power. The findings underscore the importance of administrative empowerment as a mechanism through which ethical leadership enhances job performance, offering a practical framework for evaluating and improving performance in Yemen's public companies.

title: How to Engage Regional Food Producers in Collaborative Supply Models: Lessons from Rural Bavaria
affiliations: Catholic University of Eichstaett-Ingolstadt and

detail.title: How to Engage Regional Food Producers in Collaborative Supply Models: Lessons from Rural Bavaria

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors have no conflicts of interest to declare that are relevant to the content of this article.
declarations.ethicsApproval: The study involved voluntary participation of local food producers. All participants provided informed consent prior to the interviews. Data were collected and analyzed anonymously, and any identifying information was removed or pseudonymized to ensure confidentiality. Formal ethics approval was not required according to institutional guidelines.
declarations.funderStatement: No funding was received for conducting this study.

detail.abstract: This study explores the factors influencing producer participation in regional food networks in rural areas, using the district of Landsberg am Lech in southern Germany as a case example. Against the backdrop of growing demand for regional food and the logistical challenges of integrating such products into Business-to-Business supply structures – including institutional catering – this research applies a qualitative single-case study design based on semi-structured interviews with local producers. The interviews were conceptually framed around the potential establishment of a regional food hub, enabling producers to reflect on requirements, opportunities, and challenges related to collaborative supply models. The analysis reveals three thematic dimensions shaping participation: (1) foundational conditions such as planning reliability, fair pricing, transparent governance, and logistical support; (2) supporting factors including consumer awareness and sustainability contributions; and (3) perceived challenges such as seasonal availability, additional workload, and price calculation uncertainties. The study highlights that producer engagement depends not only on logistical feasibility but also on relational and governance aspects fostering trust and fairness. In addition, the study presents practical recommendations for designing regional food networks that integrate and balance the identified structural conditions, motivational drivers and challenges to ensure credible, fair, and sustainable producer participation.

title: Authoritarian Leaders Versus Democratic Movements
affiliations: University of Bucharest

detail.title: Authoritarian Leaders Versus Democratic Movements
detail.abstract: Leaders often wield influence that surpasses structural conditions. While existing social movement literature primarily examines resources, motivations, and the policy processes within different political systems, it largely neglects the impact of variations among incumbent leaders. This paper addresses this gap by exploring how authoritarian leaders, in particular, interact with prodemocratic movements.

title: Strategic Interaction and Optimal Team Incentives: Altruism vs. Kantian Ethics

detail.title: Strategic Interaction and Optimal Team Incentives: Altruism vs. Kantian Ethics

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author has no competing interests to declare that are relevant to the content of this article.
declarations.funderStatement: This work was supported by JST SPRING, Grant Number JPMJSP2129.

detail.abstract: This paper examines how cooperative motives and production technology interact to shape optimal incentives in team production. We develop a moral hazard model with a risk-neutral principal and two agents, exploring three team configurations: (i) two selfish agents, (ii) a selfish agent with an altruistic co-worker, and (iii) a selfish agent paired with a Kantian co-worker who chooses effort according to the categorical imperative. The model explicitly allows for production technologies exhibiting either complementarity or substitutability between agents' efforts. The analysis demonstrates that the interplay between agent type and technology determines the optimal incentives. Both selfish and altruistic agents align their effort choices with the technological context-acting as strategic complements under complementarity and as substitutes under substitutability. In contrast, Kantian agents always behave as strategic complements, as they internalize the team's total output. When technology is substitutive, the presence of altruistic agents can induce negative spillovers, diminishing a selfish agent's marginal benefit and making reduced incentives optimal. Kantian coworkers, however, do not produce such negative spillovers, allowing for robust incentive schemes for selfish agents across all technological settings. These results suggest that effective incentive design must jointly consider the production environment and the cooperative motives of team members.

title: A REVIEW OF THE BUSINESS FACILITATION (MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS) ACT, 2023
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: A REVIEW OF THE BUSINESS FACILITATION (MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS) ACT, 2023
detail.abstract: The Business Facilitation (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 2023, signed into law on 10 February 2023, represents a significant legislative milestone in Nigeria's efforts to improve the ease of doing business, enhance transparency, and promote efficiency across government agencies. The Act codifies Executive Order 001 on Transparency and Efficiency in the Business Environment and introduces far-reaching amendments to 21 existing laws through its 11 sections and one schedule. This paper reviews the major provisions of the Act, including the codification of default approvals, the establishment of service level agreements, and the automation of corporate processes at the Corporate Affairs Commission. It further analyzes key amendments made to statutes such as the Companies and Allied Matters Act, Customs and Excise Management Act, Immigration Act, Industrial Training Fund Act, and the Trademarks Act, among others. The study concludes that the Act modernizes Nigeria's regulatory framework, aligns it with global best practices, and strengthens institutional accountability, though potential conflicts and implementation challenges may arise in the near future.

title: Embracing Shared Leadership: Enhancing Governance in Africa
affiliations: Durban University of Technology, IIE ADvTECH and Durban University of Technology

detail.title: Embracing Shared Leadership: Enhancing Governance in Africa
detail.abstract: This paper examines shared leadership as a transformative strategy to improve governance in Africa, addressing challenges such as political instability and economic inequality. It defines shared leadership, emphasizing collective decision-making and community empowerment, and uses case studies from 53 articles (2007-2025) to showcase successful implementations that enhance service delivery and civic engagement. The study also identifies barriers to adopting this model, including entrenched political norms, and highlights the importance of a supportive ecosystem for collaboration. Furthermore, it points out the role of technology in facilitating communication and engagement. Ultimately, it concludes that shared leadership may build more resilient governance structures and foster sustainable development by prioritizing inclusivity and collaboration.

title: From Defence Dead End to Defence Dividend? Regulatory Reflections on Developments in UK Defence Procurement Policy
affiliations: University of Nottingham

detail.title: From Defence Dead End to Defence Dividend? Regulatory Reflections on Developments in UK Defence Procurement Policy
detail.abstract: This News and Analysis Feature reviews the hotly anticipated UK Defence and Security Review. It covers a range of topical issues from a regulatory perspective. These include everything from proposals to fix a broken defence procurement system through to the use of social value and offsets as a means of achieving a "defence dividend" for the UK. The analysis is timely in light of concerns expressed about the pace at which the strategy is being implemented.

title: Rethinking Diversity: The Divergent Impacts of Relation-and Task-Oriented Diversity on Firm Performance and Risk
affiliations: , International Hellenic University (IHU), International Hellenic University (IHU) and

detail.title: Rethinking Diversity: The Divergent Impacts of Relation-and Task-Oriented Diversity on Firm Performance and Risk

declarations.funderStatement: This research project is implemented in the framework of H.F.R.I call “Basic research Financing (Horizontal support of all Sciences)” under the National Recovery and Resilience Plan “Greece 2.0” funded by the European Union – NextGenerationEU (H.F.R.I. Project Number: 15646).

detail.abstract: We investigate the impact of various board of directors diversity attributes on corporate risk (CR) and corporate financial performance (CFP). We develop a theoretical framework that draws on theories of group diversity and group performance, and we use an international sample of 12,284 firms 2000-2022. We demonstrate that relation-oriented diversity (e.g., gender, age, and nationality) does not positively affect firm outcomes, as it tends to increase risk without improving performance. In contrast, task-related diversity (e.g. tenure and expertise/skills) reduces risk and enhances performance. Therefore, firm diversity tends to be more beneficial when it emphasizes cognitive attributes over demographic characteristics. Methodologically, the findings of the relation-oriented diversity are robust across the two measuring methods (Blau and traditional operationalization) while the results for task-related diversity require a more nuanced interpretation. Our findings are robust to endogeneity, to sample selection bias, and model misspecification.

title: Do Central Banks Follow the Fed?
affiliations: University of California, Berkeley and University of California, Berkeley - Department of Economics

detail.title: Do Central Banks Follow the Fed?
detail.abstract: We study how central banks respond to U.S. monetary shocks. Using a newly constructed dataset on monetary policy meetings (the MPM-dataset), we show that emerging market (EME) central banks systematically move in tandem with the Fed, whereas advanced economy central banks do not. We attribute this heterogeneity to the asymmetric spillovers of U.S. monetary policy on firms' marginal costs. A three-bloc open-economy New Keynesian model with dominant currency pricing and partial debt dollarization reproduces these empirical patterns, highlighting that EME responses stem from the immediate impact of Fed shocks on exchange rates and, in turn, on marginal costs.

title: Signaling the Nation: How Corporate Nationalism Drives AI Innovation
affiliations: Jiangnan University, National Chiao Tung University, Jiangnan University, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Jiangnan University

detail.title: Signaling the Nation: How Corporate Nationalism Drives AI Innovation
detail.abstract: This study investigates the impact of firm-level rhetorical nationalism on artificial intelligence (AI) innovation among Chinese publicly listed companies. Leveraging an instrumental variables framework and exploiting the Sino-U.S. trade war as an exogenous shock, we find that stronger expressions of nationalism significantly enhance firms' AI patent output. Firms exhibiting higher nationalist sentiment are also more responsive to China's 2017 national AI development strategy and benefit from reduced tax liabilities and increased access to government subsidies. These effects are particularly pronounced in firms led by CEOs with IT expertise, those with lower financial constraints, state-owned enterprises, and companies explicitly committed to AI adoption. Our findings further indicate that the positive relationship is primarily driven by the "national revival" and "corporate role" dimensions of nationalism. Finally, we prove that rhetorical nationalism is positively associated with firm value.

title: Beyond Sin: A Psychological Reframing of the Seven Deadly Sins Through Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs
affiliations: La Trobe University

detail.title: Beyond Sin: A Psychological Reframing of the Seven Deadly Sins Through Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.ethicsApproval: None needed
declarations.funderStatement: N/A

detail.abstract: The purpose of this paper is to demonstrate that addictive behaviours are not the result of moral failings but rather emerge from basic human needs going unmet during key developmental phases of life. Each of the seven deadly sins will be examined in direct relation to a specific level of Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs, revealing a psychological and behavioural pattern rooted in deprivation rather than inherent vice. This paper argues that the connection between unmet needs and the manifestation of sin-like behaviours is not merely theoretical-it is observable, evidence-based, and supported by both modern psychological research and real-world examples.

title: The End of the Unipolar Moment: How Multipolar Support is Reshaping Pan-Africanism in the Sahel
affiliations: Independent Scholar

detail.title: The End of the Unipolar Moment: How Multipolar Support is Reshaping Pan-Africanism in the Sahel

declarations.declarationOfInterest: This research was conducted by an independent scholar without institutional affiliation or external funding. The manuscript was developed with assistance from Claude (Anthropic), an AI research assistant, which aided in synthesizing sources, structuring arguments, conducting literature searches, and formatting citations. All interpretations, arguments, and conclusions remain solely the responsibility of the author. The AI assistance enhanced research efficiency but did not determine the paper's analytical framework or normative positions. The author has no financial or personal relationships that influenced this study.

detail.abstract: This article advances a novel theoretical framework linking neo-colonial theory, multipolarity analysis, and American policy failures as structural enablers of Pan-African sovereignty. Departing from scholarship that treats Western hegemony and African resistance as separate phenomena, this study demonstrates that contemporary Pan-African movements succeed because of-not despite-self-inflicted American policy missteps. U.S. sanctions accelerate de-dollarization, unilateral economic nationalism undermines multilateral institutions, and military training programs paradoxically produce anti-Western coup leaders. Examining the Alliance of Sahel States (Burkina Faso, Mali, Niger), the article argues that Ibrahim Traoré operates under fundamentally different structural conditions than previous Pan-African leaders eliminated through Western intervention (Lumumba, Sankara, Gaddafi). Russian and Chinese great power protection, declining dollar hegemony, and demographic realities-the Western world comprises only 12% of global population-render continued dominance structurally untenable. The study contributes three original analyses: how U.S. military assistance produces regime opponents rather than protectors, how performative diplomacy alienates African partners through extractive logic, and why demographic imbalances make hegemony impossible. These factors explain the emergence of the first structurally viable Pan-African sovereignty project since decolonization.

title: Do key audit matter disclosures influence bank profitability and market value? Insights from emerging markets
affiliations: Putra Business School

detail.title: Do key audit matter disclosures influence bank profitability and market value? Insights from emerging markets
detail.abstract: This study examines the effect of disclosure of Key Audit Matters (KAM) on accounting and market performance of Jordanian banks listed on the Amman Stock Exchange over the period 2017-2024. The research is relevant because disclosure of audits is at the heart of winning the confidence of investors and corporate governance. The 13-bank panel data are used over the period of eight years, and fixed effects regression with robust clustered standard errors is employed. Two regressions are estimated: accounting performance in the form of return on assets (ROA) and market valuation in the form of Tobin's Q. These results are suggestive of the fact that more disclosure of KAM has been negatively and significantly connected with ROA (β =-0.176, p < 0.05), implying short-term profitability constraints, but positively and significantly connected with Tobin's Q (β = 0.285, p < 0.05), implying greater investor optimism and reduced information asymmetry. These results suggest that although KAM disclosures are not expected to directly improve profitability, they enhance market valuation through enhanced disclosure and governance. The results have policy implications for improving disclosure standards to enhance transparency and stability, and for banks to further work on strengthening the independence and qualifications of audit committees to drive performance improvements.

title: Bound by the Community Norms: Local Social Capital as an Informal Constraint on Acquisitions
affiliations: Tulane University - A.B. Freeman School of Business, The University of Sydney - Discipline of Finance, Loyola Marymount University - College of Business Administration and

detail.title: Bound by the Community Norms: Local Social Capital as an Informal Constraint on Acquisitions
detail.abstract: We examine how local social capital (LSC)-shared norms, trust, and networks within communities-shapes firms' acquisition decisions. Using county-level LSC measured at headquarters, we find that firms in high-LSC regions acquire less. Exploiting within-firm variation from headquarters relocations, instrumental variables, and the 2017 Tax Cuts and Jobs Act, we provide causal evidence. High-LSC acquirers avoid targets likely to trigger antitrust scrutiny, match with socially responsible targets, and rely less on stock payments when overvalued. Our findings highlight how community preferences operate as informal constraints on corporate decisions, with implications for corporate objectives and stakeholder orientation.

title: Robot Zombie Apocalypse: Security Implications of Wormable Exploits in Autonomous Robotics and IoT Infrastructure

detail.title: Robot Zombie Apocalypse: Security Implications of Wormable Exploits in Autonomous Robotics and IoT Infrastructure
detail.abstract: The convergence of robotics, Internet of Things (IoT), and autonomous systems introduces unprecedented security challenges that transcend traditional cybersecurity paradigms. This paper examines the UniPwn exploit affecting Unitree robotic platforms, which demonstrates the catastrophic potential of wormable vulnerabilities in autonomous systems. Through analysis of the exploit chain-comprising hardcoded cryptographic keys, insufficient handshake verification, and unsafe input handling-we reveal how attackers can achieve rootlevel privilege escalation and establish autonomous robot-torobot propagation mechanisms. The wormable nature of this exploit enables compromised robots to autonomously infect nearby devices over wireless protocols, creating what security researchers term a "robot zombie apocalypse" scenario. We examine the unique security challenges posed by robotic and IoT systems operating at the intersection of physical, wireless, and embedded domains, where traditional network security controls prove insufficient. Our analysis demonstrates that wireless communication channels-particularly Bluetooth and Wi-Fi interfaces-create attack vectors bypassing conventional network segmentation. For critical infrastructure applications employing autonomous inspection robots, drones, and unmanned vehicles, these vulnerabilities present existential risks enabling adversaries to weaponize trusted automation systems against the infrastructure they were designed to protect. We propose a comprehensive security framework addressing firmware security, wireless protocol hardening, physical-cyber boundary protection, and defense-in-depth strategies specific to autonomous robotic systems. The findings emphasize that securing robotic and IoT infrastructure requires fundamentally rethinking security architectures to account for mobility, wireless communication, physical interaction capabilities, and autonomous behavior that distinguish these systems from traditional IT assets.

title: Beyond WEIRD Bias: Why Token-Based Legal AI Cannot Model Post-Colonial Compliance Dynamics

detail.title: Beyond WEIRD Bias: Why Token-Based Legal AI Cannot Model Post-Colonial Compliance Dynamics

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no financial or commercial conflicts of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This research uses exclusively publicly available official government statistics and legal documents. No human participants were involved, no personal data was collected, and no ethics approval was required. All data sources are cited with URLs to enable verification and reproducibility.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. The author maintains independent legal practice in Buenos Aires unrelated to legal AI product development or consulting.

detail.abstract:
Joseph Henrich's The WEIRDest People in the World (2020) demonstrates that Western psychology—individualistic, impersonally prosocial, guilt-based—emerged from the Catholic Church's Marriage and Family Program (400-1200 CE) dissolving extended kin networks. This historical accident, affecting 12% of humanity, enabled specific institutional forms: impersonal markets, rule-based bureaucracy, constitutional governance. The remaining 88% retained relationship-based, kin-intensive, shame-oriented psychology and corresponding particularistic institutions.

This paper demonstrates that legal AI systems trained on WEIRD legal corpora cannot serve non-WEIRD jurisdictions because they encode institutional assumptions requiring WEIRD psychology. The formal/informal compliance gap—divergence between law-as-written and law-as-enforced—averages 5.4% in WEIRD societies versus 31.2% in non-WEIRD societies (difference: 25.8 percentage points, p < 0.0001, Cohen's d = 3.749). This gap is not "weak institutions" but rational adaptation: populations lacking WEIRD psychology cannot sustain WEIRD institutional forms without systematic discount.

We formalize this through successive multiplicative layers: behavioral framing (Layer 1, ≈12%) × psychology-institution mismatch (Layer 2, ≈3× in non-WEIRD contexts) × institutional volatility (Layer 2b) = compound divergence. Token-based language models cannot represent this structure—they fragment trans-jurisdictional concepts, lack explicit parameters for psychology-institution mismatch, and cannot perform counterfactual reasoning.

Building on this author's IusSpace and Iusmorfos frameworks (87.4% prediction accuracy across 18 reforms in 13 countries), we introduce LegalGapDB (first systematic database documenting formal/informal divergence) and París-SCM: a mixture-of-experts concept-based architecture achieving 81% accuracy on specialist legal queries versus 67% for monolithic models and 58% for GPT-4. This represents the first worldwide adaptation of token-free architectures from image generation to legal reasoning, providing operational solution for legal AI serving the 88% of humanity under non-WEIRD institutional arrangements.

title: Green Disclosure or Green Hushing? The Impact of Corporate Environmental Sustainability Communication on Social Media Engagement
affiliations: ,  and McGill University

detail.title: Green Disclosure or Green Hushing? The Impact of Corporate Environmental Sustainability Communication on Social Media Engagement

keywords: social identity theory Environmental Sustainability Communication and Social Media Engagement

detail.abstract: Social media has become a key channel for companies to communicate sustainability initiatives. However, given the polarized public attitudes toward sustainability, the effectiveness of such communication remains uncertain, and research on the impact of corporate sustainability communications via social media is limited. Grounded in social identity theory and utilizing large-scale observational data from X, we find a counterintuitive result: corporate sustainability communications on social media are associated with an average 29.11% decrease in engagement volume across companies’ regular communications. Interestingly, however, we find that response messages (as opposed to broadcast messages) can offset this adverse effect. We further show that this negative effect is influenced by a company’s social media characteristics. By revealing the unintended negative consequences of sustainability communication on social media and identifying mitigating factors, this study extends the literature on sustainable marketing and suggests that companies take a more cautious and strategic approach to promoting sustainability.

title: Technology Law Chapter 4: Perspectives
affiliations: University of Wisconsin Law School and University of Richmond School of Law, Yale University - Yale Information Society Project

detail.title: Technology Law Chapter 4: Perspectives
detail.abstract:
Based on years of experience teaching the subject, we have produced a first draft of a “Technology Law” coursebook. It teases out fundamental concepts, introduces our methodology for resolving tech-fostered legal uncertainties, and identifies the strengths and weaknesses of different regulatory choices. Through a mixture of readings, exercises, and discussion questions, it helps readers develop facility in:

- Recognizing the recurring techlaw and policy questions and discerning the application, normative, and institutional uncertainties associated with a particular technology;
- Working through the process of resolving legal uncertainties, which includes consciously selecting a regulatory approach, identifying legally salient characteristics and relevant analogies, and weighing the benefits and drawbacks of various regulatory choices (law-by-analogy, creating new law, or reconfiguring legal institutions); and
- Developing familiarity with employing and countering common rhetorical strategies for advancing, opposing, or shaping regulation.

This course is designed to be accessible and useful to all students, regardless of career interests or prior experience with technology. New technologies challenge every area of the law, and the regulatory and rhetorical strategies we’ll explore are transferable across subjects.

This posting includes Chapter 4: Perspectives. Future chapters will be posted bi-monthly.

We welcome feedback at the link included in the document; additional chapters will be updated regularly. If you are interested in teaching from this text, in whole or in part, please let us know, as we would be happy to share our class notes and slides.

title: Generative AIs and the Hidden Cost of Intelligence: A Multidisciplinary Review of LLMs Progress, Resource Consumption and Path to a Sustainable Future
affiliations: Virtual University of Pakistan, Virtual University of Pakistan and Virtual University of Pakistan - Department of Management Sciences

detail.title: Generative AIs and the Hidden Cost of Intelligence: A Multidisciplinary Review of LLMs Progress, Resource Consumption and Path to a Sustainable Future

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflict of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: All authors are agreed.

publicationDetails.detailsText:
Annual Methodological Archive Research Review, Volume 3, Issue No.9, Pp. 84-107.

detail.abstract: The rapid advancement of Large Language Models (LLMs) and Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) has reshaped technological, business and social environments. Though the models-GPT-4, GPT-5, Claude and others-have shown unparalleled abilities in automation, creative work and decision-making, they have placed enormous burdens on natural resources such as energy, water and computational infrastructure raw materials. This paper offers a multidisciplinary analysis with integrated views from environmental science, computer engineering, economics and business information systems perspective. The research analyzes the environmental externalities of LLMs training and deployment, and measures resource usage patterns and places them in context of global sustainability objectives. Methodologically, the study utilizes a mixed review framework by incorporating systematic literature review and secondary data analysis from peerreviewed journals in ScienceDirect, Taylor & Francis, Wiley Online, IEEE, MDPI, SpringerLink, SAGE, Emerald and other trustworthy databases. The findings show that the growth of GenAI is happening at an unsustainable level unless checked by strategic interventions on infrastructure efficiency, policy regulation and corporate environment responsibility. It is suggested to imperatively reconcile AI innovation with the circular economy and carbon-neutral computing principles to guarantee that intelligence augmentation is not at the cost of planetary well-being.

title: AI-Driven UX Design: How Technology Enhances Human-Centered Experiences
affiliations: UI/UX Designer & Researcher

detail.title: AI-Driven UX Design: How Technology Enhances Human-Centered Experiences

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have influenced the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This research involved voluntary participation in surveys and interviews with professionals. No sensitive personal data was collected, and all participants provided informed consent. Formal institutional ethics approval was not required for this study.

detail.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming the design landscape, redefining how user experiences (UX) are conceptualized, prototyped, and delivered. This research explores the intersection of AI and UX design by analyzing how AI Engineers and UX Designers perceive, adopt, and collaborate through AI-based design generation tools. The study employed a mixed-method research methodology combining quantitative surveys and qualitative interviews to understand adoption behavior, collaboration patterns, and ethical considerations. Findings reveal that while AI enhances speed, efficiency, and ideation, it still lacks empathy, contextual understanding, and creative nuance—qualities inherent to human designers. Both groups agree that AI serves best as a co-pilot rather than a replacement. The study concludes that the future of UX design lies in human–AI co-creation, where technology augments human creativity rather than automating it.

title: Less to Process, More to Express: The Impact of AI-Generated Summaries on Review Diversity
affiliations: University of Florida - Warrington College of Business Administration, University of Florida - Warrington College of Business Administration, University of Florida - Warrington College of Business and University of Florida - Warrington College of Business Administration

detail.title: Less to Process, More to Express: The Impact of AI-Generated Summaries on Review Diversity
detail.abstract: As generative AI becomes increasingly embedded in online marketplaces, understanding its influence on consumer activities becomes critical. In today's online marketplaces, consumers contributing reviews are particularly important, as consumer review systems now serve as a primary channel for sharing and obtaining product information. Effectively managing consumer review systems in the context of expanding generative AI applications requires a clear understanding of how these tools shape review contributions. Yet, despite the widespread adoption of generative AI tools, empirical evidence of their impact on consumer-generated content remains limited. Our study addresses this gap by exploiting Amazon's rollout of AI-generated summaries (AIGS) on product pages as a natural experiment. Contrary to the prevailing narrative that AI might homogenize voices, we find that the introduction of AIGS significantly increases the diversity of consumer reviews. This effect is consistent with the notion that by condensing prior reviews into concise and informative summaries, AIGS reduces the cognitive effort required to process existing information, enabling contributors to focus on offering more distinctive experiences and insights. Moderation analyses reveal that this positive effect on review diversity is particularly pronounced for products with high rating dispersion or limited product descriptions, contexts in which assimilating prior reviews typically demands greater cognitive effort. These findings support the interpretation that AIGS fosters review diversity by alleviating cognitive load in information processing. Our findings advance the theory on generative AI, human-AI interaction, and user-generated content, while offering practical guidance for platform managers: thoughtfully designed AI features can amplify diverse perspectives, enriching the informational value of reviews.

title: Risk Management as a Strategic Bridge: Aligning Cybersecurity Architecture with Business Objectives in Modern Organizations

detail.title: Risk Management as a Strategic Bridge: Aligning Cybersecurity Architecture with Business Objectives in Modern Organizations
detail.abstract: Cybersecurity has evolved from a purely technical discipline into a critical business strategic imperative that directly influences organizational performance, profitability, and resilience. This paper examines the role of risk management as the essential bridge connecting technical cybersecurity controls with organizational business objectives. Through analysis of contemporary cyber incidents, including the 2021 Colonial Pipeline ransomware attack, and recent empirical research on vulnerability management and organizational adaptation, we demonstrate that mature risk management practices enable organizations to allocate resources efficiently, prioritize protection efforts effectively, and maintain business continuity in an evolving threat landscape. We identify critical barriers to effective risk management implementation, particularly in small and medium enterprises (SMEs), where limited security literacy among decision-makers results in misaligned investments and inadequate protection. Our analysis reveals that organizations with mature risk management programs demonstrate superior budget allocation effectiveness and enhanced business resilience compared to those treating cybersecurity as purely a cost center. We propose a framework for integrating risk-based thinking into cybersecurity architecture that balances protection, usability, and cost considerations while accommodating emerging technologies such as generative artificial intelligence. The findings emphasize that risk management represents not merely a compliance exercise but rather a fundamental strategic capability that enables organizations of all sizes to align cybersecurity investments with mission-critical business outcomes.

title: Market Reactions as a Macroeconomic Barometer: Evidence from the TCJA
affiliations: University of Utah - School of Accounting and Information Systems and Northeastern University

detail.title: Market Reactions as a Macroeconomic Barometer: Evidence from the TCJA
detail.abstract: We develop a new method to estimate the effects of the 2017 Tax Cuts and Jobs Act (TCJA) on GDP that can be applied to both past and future reforms. Evaluating such reforms is difficult because provisions are broad and interrelated. To address this challenge, we combine abnormal stock returns during TCJA legislative windows with the pre-existing geographic distribution of firms to construct a county-level measure of exposure. Linking this measure to real outcomes, we estimate that the TCJA raised GDP by 1.8 percent, through higher investment, with gains concentrated in business income and older, wealthier counties.

title: A Study on the Koreanization Influence in Northeast India: A Review
affiliations: Manipur International University, Jawaharlal Nehru University and Assam University - Department of Business Administration

detail.title: A Study on the Koreanization Influence in Northeast India: A Review
detail.abstract: In recent years, the phenomenon of the Korean Wave has garnered global attention due to its expansive cultural influence and the rapid acceptance of Korean culture, a process termed "Koreanization." This study addresses the research question of why the Korean Wave is being widely embraced despite the lack of direct historical interactions, unlike Japan's influence during World War II or Britain's colonial impact. To offer a comprehensive response, the study proposes a systematic review of existing Korean cultural research using the Dimensions database, followed by an analysis in VOSviewer as its first objective. The second objective focuses on identifying the hierarchical factors that drive the spread of the Korean Wave in Northeast Asia and beyond. The study employs a qualitative approach, leveraging rich literature and theoretical frameworks to uncover the underlying causes of this cultural phenomenon. Key findings suggest that the rapid acceptance of Korean culture is facilitated by cultural similarities, familial structures, daily practices, and the influence of Generation Z. Furthermore, the study highlights the subtle yet significant role of Western influences, which have been mediated through Korean adaptations. A crucial takeaway from this study is the importance of academic engagement in promoting Korean culture, advocating for its introduction at the primary education level to ensure effective cultural transmission.

title: TACKLE: Time-based Access Control and Key delegation for Letter of credit Ecosystems
affiliations: , Lecturer, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: TACKLE: Time-based Access Control and Key delegation for Letter of credit Ecosystems
detail.abstract: Letters of Credit (L/Cs) are essential for international trade, but traditional systems struggle with security, efficiency, and access control. To address these challenges, we propose TACKLE, a new framework that combines identity-based encryption (IBE) with blockchain technology. TACKLE offers advanced features like time-based access control and hierarchical key delegation, making it ideal for complex international trade workflows. Our framework significantly improves document verification and access management while maintaining strong security. We tested TACKLE's performance and found it to be efficient, with quick key generation times (68-74 milliseconds) and fast encryption (3.933 to 8.333 seconds). Network latency was stable at 2-8 milliseconds across different data sizes. Compared to RSA, TACKLE generated keys 34.2% faster while using similar system resources. Our results show that TACKLE effectively balances security with efficiency, making it suitable for typical L/C documents up to 10MB. With its strong security features and performance, TACKLE is a promising solution for modernizing international trade finance.

title: Energy Funds and Energy Taxes as Stabilizers against Energy Price Shocks
affiliations: Singapore Management University - School of Economics

detail.title: Energy Funds and Energy Taxes as Stabilizers against Energy Price Shocks
detail.abstract: This paper explores the role of active fiscal intervention in the events of energy price shocks. The analysis encompasses a number of demand and supply shocks to the energy market thanks to the endogenous energy sector with convex costs. The fiscal intervention comprises an energy fund and energy taxes on households and producers. Our findings indicate a welfare improvement and smaller adverse responses of the business cycle compared to a reference model without these fiscal features. The results provide theoretical support for the effectiveness of energy fund and energy taxes in business cycle stabilization against energy price shocks.

title: The Self-Inflicted Decline of American Hegemony: How Policy Failures Enable Multipolar Alternatives
affiliations: Independent Scholar

detail.title: The Self-Inflicted Decline of American Hegemony: How Policy Failures Enable Multipolar Alternatives

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no financial or personal conflicts of interest. This manuscript was prepared with assistance from Claude (Anthropic AI) for literature review, citation formatting, structural organization, and prose refinement. All intellectual contributions, arguments, theoretical framework, case selection, analysis, and conclusions are the author's own original work. All factual claims have been independently verified by the author against primary and secondary sources.

keywords: Global South sovereignty JEL Classification: F51

detail.abstract: This article examines how American foreign policy paradoxically creates structural conditions for its own circumvention. Contrary to analyses attributing hegemonic decline primarily to rising competitors, I demonstrate that contemporary multipolarity emerges significantly from self-inflicted U.S. policy failures. I identify four "paradoxical mechanisms" through which policies designed to enforce compliance instead accelerate alternatives: sanctions drive de-dollarization, military training produces adversarial leadership, performative diplomacy alienates partners, and institutional undermining destroys frameworks that secured hegemony. Venezuela provides comprehensive empirical test. Despite "maximum pressure" sanctions explicitly designed to produce regime change, Venezuela survived through multipolar partnerships (Russian military cooperation, Chinese economic support, Iranian technical assistance) and systematic de-dollarization. The Atlantic Council concluded that sanctions "did not serve US interests" and "principally benefitted adversaries." The Alliance of Sahel States validates Venezuelan mechanisms across different regional context: U.S.-trained officers led coups expelling Western forces, then established Russian/Chinese alternatives. I argue that when three conditions converge-multipolar backing, de-dollarization infrastructure, and Western credibility decline-resistance transitions from structurally impossible to demonstrably viable. Demographic reality (Western nations comprising 12% of global population) makes continued dominance structurally untenable. American policies have not created this constraint but have accelerated recognition of it, systematically undermining the institutional credibility and financial leverage that once enabled dominance despite demographic asymmetry.

title: Beyond volatility of volatility: Decomposing the informational content of VVIX
affiliations: HEC Montreal - Department of Decision Sciences, Simon Fraser University and HEC Montreal - Department of Decision Sciences

detail.title: Beyond volatility of volatility: Decomposing the informational content of VVIX
detail.abstract: This study investigates the informational content of the VVIX, traditionally viewed as a proxy for the S&P 500 index's volatility of the volatility (VOV). We show that this interpretation is incomplete: the VVIX also embeds a long-run variance (LRV) component. To establish this result, we first demonstrate that regressions of squared VVIX on VOV proxies gain substantial explanatory power once LRV measures are incorporated. We then develop a tractable theoretical framework linking VVIX to three risk drivers-the instantaneous variance, LRV, and VOV-and show that the VVIX loads on both VOV and LRV. Our empirical analysis reveals that VVIX dynamics are dominated by LRV in calm markets, but by VOV during financial stress. We further show that these variance components explain option returns in distinct markets: S&P 500 index option straddles load on the instantaneous variance and LRV, while VIX option straddles load on the VOV. Taken together, our results redefine the role of the VVIX, establishing it as a measure of both VOV and LRV uncertainty, with important implications for how it should be read and used by finance practitioners.

title: The Gatekeeping Expert's Dilemma
affiliations: Columbia University - Columbia Business School

detail.title: The Gatekeeping Expert's Dilemma
detail.abstract: This paper studies how experts with veto power—gatekeeping experts—influence agents through communication. Their expertise helps agents' decisions, while veto power provides discipline. Gatekeepers face a dilemma: transparent communication can invite gaming, while opacity wastes expertise. How can gatekeeping experts guide behavior without being gamed? Many economic settings feature this tradeoff, including bank stress tests, environmental regulations, and financial auditing. Using financial auditing as the primary setting, I show that strategic vagueness resolves this dilemma: by revealing just enough to prevent the manager from inflating the report, the auditor guides the manager while minimizing opportunities for manipulation. This theoretical lens provides a novel rationale for why auditors predominantly accept clients' financial reports. Comparative statics reveals that greater gatekeeper independence or expertise sometimes dampens communication. This paper shows how communication and veto power together make gatekeepers effective.

title: Learning the Exact SABR Model
affiliations: Intesa SanPaolo SpA, Prometeia and University of Bologna

detail.title: Learning the Exact SABR Model
detail.abstract:
The SABR model is a cornerstone of interest rate volatility modeling, but its practical application relies heavily on the analytical approximation by Hagan et al., whose accuracy deteriorates for high volatility, long maturities, and out-of-the-money options, admitting arbitrage. While machine learning approaches have been proposed to overcome these limitations, they have often been limited by simplified SABR dynamics or a lack of systematic validation against the full spectrum of market conditions. 
We develop a novel SABR DNN, a specialized Artificial Deep Neural Network (DNN) architecture that learns the true SABR stochastic dynamics using an unprecedented large training dataset (more than 200 million points) of interest rate Cap/Floor volatility surfaces, including very long maturities (30Y) and extreme strikes consistently with market quotations. Our dataset is obtained via high-precision unbiased Monte Carlo simulation of a special scaled shifted-SABR stochastic dynamics, which allows dimensional reduction without any loss of generality. Our SABR DNN provides arbitrage-free calibration of real market volatility surfaces and Caps/Floors prices for any maturity and strike with negligible computational effort and without retraining across business dates. 
Our results fully address the gaps in the previous machine learning SABR literature in a systematic and self-consistent way, and can be extended to cover any interest rate European options in different rate tenors and currencies, thus establishing a comprehensive functional SABR framework that can be adopted for daily trading and risk management activities.

title: Sustainability Certificates and Relationship Lending
affiliations: Hochschule für Finanzwirtschaft und Management, RWTH Aachen University, , Leibniz Institute for Financial Research SAFE and RWTH Aachen University - Department of Finance

detail.title: Sustainability Certificates and Relationship Lending

declarations.funderStatement: This work was created as part of the project “LIFE21-CET-MAINSTREAM-CONFESS/101077584”. The project was funded by the European Union under the LIFE programme. Views and opinions expressed are however those of the author(s) only and do not necessarily reflect those of the European Union or CINEA. Neither the European Union nor the granting authority can be held responsible for them.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the important role of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and their business relationships with credit institutions in the context of the transformation toward a more sustainable economy. We survey 107 corporate client consultants or credit analysts of banks to infer banks’ reaction on hypothetical scenarios where a sustainability certification process for SMEs is established. We find that if they are not required to include sustainability information in the credit granting process, credit institutions consider negative sustainability information less for their relationship clients than for new clients. However, once a regulation is introduced that restricts the credit granting process for non-sustainable companies, the treatment of non-sustainable new clients and existing clients converges compared to their sustainable counterparts. This effect is particularly pronounced for the fundamental decision upon granting new loans or not, while credit conditions for relationship and new clients are more similar even in a situation without banking regulation based on the newly disseminated SME sustainability information. Our results highlight the role of sustainability certificates in enhancing access to financing for sustainable transformation among SMEs.

title: Can ESG Strategies Drive Firm Value Growth in the MENA Region?
affiliations: , The British University in Egypt and The British University in Egypt

detail.title: Can ESG Strategies Drive Firm Value Growth in the MENA Region?
detail.abstract: Cross-industry and crosscountry evidence from the ESG-firm value literature indicates no consensus on the ESG performance impact on corporate financial performance. Stemming from the ongoing debate over whether ESG principles enhance or hinder value creation, this study investigates the effect of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) performance on firm value through three proxies: Tobin's Q (TQ), Price to Book ratio (PB), and Price to Earnings ratio (PE). Using a crosscountry and cross-sectoral comparative approach, the study employs static and dynamic panel regression analyses, along with principal component analysis, to test the hypothesized relationships across nine MENA region countries and ten sectors between 2017 and 2022. To the best of the authors' knowledge, this is the first study to examine ESG's impact on TQ, PB, and PE while offering a comparative analysis in the MENA region. Empirical results reveal a significantly positive relationship between ESG scores and firm value using TQ and PB ratios, but this relationship is insignificant with the PE ratio. This study contributes to the ESG and financial decision-making literature, providing insights for investors on portfolio optimization and sustainable investing. The findings offer recommendations that further benefit businesses, policymakers, and decision-makers in enhancing their understanding of ESG implications.

title: Optimal Self-Protection in Peer-to-Peer Insurance: The Dual Role of Risk Sharing
affiliations: , , KU Leuven, Department Accounting, Finance and Insurance and Southern University of Science and Technology

detail.title: Optimal Self-Protection in Peer-to-Peer Insurance: The Dual Role of Risk Sharing
detail.abstract: This paper examines optimal self-protection in peer-to-peer (P2P) insurance. We find that while P2P risk-sharing inherently encourages preventive effort compared to classical insurance, it also introduces a free-rider problem because effort costs are unshareable. To solve this, we integrate a tontine fund into the P2P framework. We prove that the resulting P2P-tontine hybrid enhances participants' effort levels without imposing additional costs, offering a practical mechanism to improve risk prevention in decentralized insurance.

title: Rapid Assessment of Ethiopian Media during the Transition Period

detail.title: Rapid Assessment of Ethiopian Media during the Transition Period

declarations.ethicsApproval: The study adhers all the ethical issues.

detail.abstract: The purpose of the rapid assessment was to form a basis for discussions among key stakeholders in media and politics who may be interested in the media's role during Ethiopia's transition. As it is known, after many challenges for more than two decades, the Ethiopian media are now relatively free and open. This is happening in connection with the coming to power of Dr Abiy Ahmed in April 2018. Soon after his appointment, he promised to bring changes to the country. One of the changes that he promised was to make the media free. Laws that can be described as draconian, for example, the Anti-terrorism Law and the Mass Media and Access to Information Proclamation, are now under revision. Media policy is also under discussion. The New Media Council, which has started functioning to promote self-regulation, is now operational. Accountability of the public media sectors is now shifted from the executive body to the parliament. All these initiatives have been accomplished in a remarkably short period. However, the question of how far the media is playing its role, for instance, in promoting peace and reconciliation, and democratisation has not been assessed scientifically. Hence, the rapid assessment was initiated to critically look at the role of media during transition and trigger discussion among key media stakeholders and the government.

title: Superstition and Labor Supply: Evidence from 16 Million Ride-sharing Transactions
affiliations: Renmin University of China - School of Agricultural Economics and Rural Development, Peking University - Guanghua School of Management, Renmin University of China - School of Applied Economics and Zhejiang University

detail.title: Superstition and Labor Supply: Evidence from 16 Million Ride-sharing Transactions
detail.abstract: We provide the first evidence on how superstition distorts labor supply. Using ridehailing transaction data from a major city in China, we find that drivers are 2.47 percentage points less likely to work on inauspicious days designated by the Huang-Li, an ancient Chinese almanac, and complete about 0.61 fewer rides, representing a 4.1% decline relative to the mean. These reductions persist after accounting for intertemporal substitution, as only part of the lost supply shifts to adjacent days. Demand-side analysis shows no decline in consumer orders, while prices rise modestly, confirming that the contraction originates from supply. The superstition effect is amplified on adverseweather days and among drivers from more religious hometowns, but attenuated among those from hometowns with stronger marriage-market pressures. Back-of-the-envelope estimates suggest an annual labor supply loss of roughly 2.08 billion USD nationwide, underscoring how cultural beliefs can impede modern labor markets in developing countries.

title: Feasibility of Blockchain-Based Intermediary Alternatives: An Economic Analysis
affiliations: University of Zurich - Department of Informantics, University of Zurich and University of Zurich

detail.title: Feasibility of Blockchain-Based Intermediary Alternatives: An Economic Analysis
detail.abstract: This paper develops an economic model analyzing the feasibility and welfare implications of replacing profit-maximizing intermediaries with welfare-maximizing consortium blockchain platforms. We investigate how platform governance, technology maturity, and competitive strategies interact to determine market outcomes, particularly under price coherence constraints. Three main results emerge. First, welfare-maximizing platforms never voluntarily impose price coherence, as this introduces inefficiencies reducing social welfare compared to first-best outcomes achievable without such constraints. Second, when blockchain consortiums enter markets where traditional intermediaries enforce price coherence, they can significantly improve welfare through rebate competition etc. strategies, even with inferior technology. Consortium platforms transform traditional markups into competitive advantages, forcing intermediary fee reductions and mitigating welfare distortions. Third, blockchain adoption decisions involve fundamental trade-offs between governance advantages and technology maturity. The analysis shows that adoption thresholds for blockchain platforms are substantially lower in markets characterized by high traditional intermediary markups and price coherence enforcement. These findings provide decision frameworks for market participants and generate testable implications for platform competition, pricing strategies, and technology adoption in intermediated markets.

title: Reallocating Environmental Risk
affiliations: UC Davis School of Law and Albany Law School

detail.title: Reallocating Environmental Risk

declarations.declarationOfInterest: NA
declarations.ethicsApproval: NA
declarations.funderStatement: Supported by the Environmental Law Collaborative.

detail.abstract: Environmental law relies on a predict-and-mitigate model. Regulators predict the impacts of proposed actions and then undertaking mitigation to reduce or eliminate those impacts. Two sources of error complicate that approach: bad predictions and failed mitigation. Predictions often understate the scale of impacts and miss some impacts entirely. Mitigation actions often fail to produce the promised benefits, either because they are not completed or because they simply do not function as anticipated. Insufficient monitoring and enforcement mean these two problems often go uncorrected. Failed mitigation and incorrect environmental predictions create three serious problems, undercutting the foundational predict-and-mitigate model of environmental law. First, these errors produce worse environmental outcomes than those approved by permitting decisions. Examples include lost ecosystem services, species extinction, and negative human health impacts. Second, these errors produce distributional justice issues. Permittees seldom bear responsibility for their errors, so our current system essentially allocates the risk of errors to the public. In other words, when mitigation fails, or if the environmental impacts of a project are more significant than predicted, the environment and the public, not project proponents, pay the price. Third, because permittees do not bear the risk of these errors, they are externalizing significant financial risks associated their actions. Externalizing these costs creates a market distortion, leading permittees to pursue projects that would not make economic sense if all costs were considered. This article seeks to reallocate the risks of bad predictions and failed mitigation from the public to the permittees themselves using financial assurance tools. Financial assurances, used extensively in land use decisions, require project proponents to secure enough future funding to pay for new mitigation, should the planned mitigation fail. As we show, tools like performance bonds, cash escrows, letters of credit or insurance can and should be used to reallocate risks created by these errors in permitting decisions. From a variety of real-world risk reallocation examples, we extract best practices in financial assurance risk reallocation and apply those lessons to two current, high-profile environmental controversies: California's Bay-Delta Plan and federal National Environmental Policy Act reform. This analysis shows environmental risk reallocation will produce better environmental outcomes, ensure that permittees bear responsibility for predict-and-mitigate errors, and internalize the cost of risk, leading potential permittees to make better decisions about which projects to pursue.

title: AI-Powered Climate Intelligence Systems for Disaster Resilience in Asia-Pacific: A Knowledge Management Framework
affiliations: Jahangirnagar University

detail.title: AI-Powered Climate Intelligence Systems for Disaster Resilience in Asia-Pacific: A Knowledge Management Framework

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no personal or financial relationships with any other people or organizations that may have, or could be perceived to have, influenced this study.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study did not require ethical approval or informed consent as it involved no human subjects, in accordance with institutional guidelines. Acknowledgements: I acknowledge the contributions of climate scientists, AI researchers, and community practitioners across Asia-Pacific nations whose collaborative efforts advance climate resilience.
declarations.funderStatement: Funding: None. This research did not receive any specific grant from funding agencies in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: The Asia-Pacific region boasts unparalleled climatic exposures with 45% of global disaster occurrences happening annually. This article critically examines the intersection of Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML), and Big Data analytics in developing climate intelligence systems tailored for Asia-Pacific environments. We propose an inclusive Knowledge Management System (KMS) model that transforms AIbased insights into actionable intelligence in disaster readiness. Our analysis demonstrates the promise of AI-driven early warning systems to reduce disaster-related mortality by up to 30% while improving forecast accuracy for floods, cyclones, and droughts prevalent in the region. The architecture addresses the fundamental challenges of data interoperability, digital divide, and community-level knowledge dissemination in heterogeneous Asia-Pacific nations. The earth is an interconnected system, constantly generating massive quantities of data. Satellite imagery captures ice cap, sea level, and vegetation cover alterations. Ground sensor networks meticulously monitor temperature, humidity, rain, and atmospheric gas concentrations. Marine buoys report ocean current and sea life. Such a flood of information, all too frequently unstructured and heterogeneous, is the fodder for AI and ML. Traditional analysis methods may not be able to cope with, aggregate, and yield meaningful patterns from such vast amounts. That is where AI comes in.

title: Capital Allocation Under Overboarded Directors
affiliations: University of Denver and Bentley University - Department of Finance

detail.title: Capital Allocation Under Overboarded Directors
detail.abstract: This paper examines how board busyness affects corporate abnormal investment, defined as the deviation from investment predicted by a Q-theory model. While busy directors may face time constraints, they can also bring expertise, reputational capital, and valuable external networks. Using multiple measures of board busyness, we find that firms with busier boards exhibit significantly lower levels of abnormal investment. This effect is entirely driven by a reduction in underinvestment, suggesting that busy directors help firms better identify and pursue positive NPV investment opportunities. The effect is stronger when busy directors have industry-specific expertise, indicating that relevant knowledge enhances board effectiveness. We also observe a nonlinear, U-shaped pattern in the relationship between board busyness and underinvestment, with benefits tapering off and reversing beyond 5 busy directors per board. Using local firm density and the presence of female directors as instrumental variables, we establish a causal link between board busyness and underinvestment. Overall, these findings highlight the role of busy directors in improving capital allocation, while offering early evidence on potential diminishing returns to board busyness.

title: Statistical Analysis Report-II

detail.title: Statistical Analysis Report-II

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflict of interest
declarations.ethicsApproval: Approval was taken from the participants for this study.
declarations.funderStatement: The author didn't receive any external funding for this study

detail.abstract:
As part of my practicum teaching, I was assigned to teach Bangla in class Eight (Kha section) and English 2nd paper in class six (Ka section) at Ahmadia Model High School. I had the opportunity to teach secondary students and get a practical knowledge of teaching in real life. Teaching is not only about teaching and grading but also about teacher's own learning process and conducting research to improve his/her teaching strategies or solving any problem related to teaching. In my opinion, a good teacher focuses on students' learning more than teaching and testing. He/she helps students to achieve their social and emotional skills which also helps their daily life and have impacts on academic performances. Standard assessment system is also an important part of teaching-learning program, which determines students academic excellence.

During my internship period, I conducted two tests for each subject I was assigned to teach in regular classes. In this statistical report, I will attempt to identify students' strengths and weaknesses using some basic theoretical formulas and standard score analysis. I will compare the pre and post test results to measure the overall academic performance of the students.

In this report, I will analyze the test results and scores of my assigned subject, English 2nd Paper, for class Six.

title: Market-Based Variance of Market Portfolio and of Entire Market
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Market-Based Variance of Market Portfolio and of Entire Market
detail.abstract: We present the unified market-based description of returns and variances of the trades with shares of a particular security, of the trades with shares of all securities in the market, and of the trades with the market portfolio. We consider the investor who doesn't trade the shares of his portfolio he collected at time t0 in the past. The investor observes the time series of the current trades with all securities made in the market during the averaging interval. The investor may convert these time series into the time series that model the trades with all securities as the trades with a single security and into the time series that model the trades with the market portfolio as the trades with a single security. That establishes the same description of the returns and variances of the trades with a single security, the trades with all securities in the market, and the market portfolio. We show that the market-based variance, which accounts for the impact of random change of the volumes of consecutive trades with securities, takes the form of Markowitz's (1952) portfolio variance if the volumes of consecutive trades with all market securities are assumed constant. That highlights that Markowitz's (1952) variance ignores the effects of random volumes of consecutive trades. We compare the market-based variances of the market portfolio and of the trades with all market securities, consider the importance of the duration of the averaging interval, and explain the economic obstacles that limit the accuracy of the predictions of the returns and variances at best by Gaussian distributions. The same methods describe the returns and variances of any portfolio and the trades with its securities.

title: Do Liquidity Management Dynamics Translate to Efficiency of the Nigerian Bank? A Data Envelopment Analysis Approach
affiliations: University of Calabar- Department of Banking & Finance, University of Calabar, University of Calabar (UNICAL) - Department of Banking and Finance and University of Uyo (UNIUYO)

detail.title: Do Liquidity Management Dynamics Translate to Efficiency of the Nigerian Bank? A Data Envelopment Analysis Approach
detail.abstract: Short-term financial health is essential for any business to stay stable, face economic challenges, and pursue growth opportunities. This study examines the impact of liquidity management strategies, including the Loan to Deposit Ratio (LDR), Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR), liquid assets to ratio (LATR), and overall liquidity, on the financial performance of banks in Nigeria, as measured by Constant Return to Scale Efficiency. Secondary data from the Central Bank of Nigeria's bulletin were analyzed. The research uses Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) multiple regression analysis to estimate the model. Results indicate that CRSE is negatively related to LASFR but positively related to LR, LTDR, and CRR, highlighting implications for improving asset quality and policy development to decrease non-performing loans, as recommended for the Nigerian banking sector. The finding that an increase in CRR positively impacts banks' performance aligns with Liquidity Preference Theory. This suggests that, in our context, banks' liquidity management strategies respond to changes in CRR by adjusting their liquid assets, likely anticipating shifts in interbank lending rates. This proactive approach to liquidity management helps improve financial performance.

title: Why Venture Later? Incentives, Learning, and Industry Allocation in VC Funds *
affiliations: Stockholm School of Economics - Stockholm School of Economics - Swedish House of Finance, Students

detail.title: Why Venture Later? Incentives, Learning, and Industry Allocation in VC Funds *
detail.abstract: Why do VC funds delay entry into high-uncertainty sectors? I structurally estimate a dynamic model with two frictions (an LP-GP scale wedge and a GP-entrepreneur information wedge) embedded in diffusion that separates learning from adoption. Fund-1 exploration and monitoring map into Fund-2 portfolio composition and scale. Using simulated method of moments on matched fund pairs, I find: (i) the information wedge depresses composition by killing early signals; (ii) the LP-GP wedge rations investment in hot markets, with dominance reversing in cold markets. Counterfactuals imply combined frictions reduce surplus by about $37 billion (approximately 2.8% of VC and 12% of new-sector capital). Policies targeting composition (exploration-linked carry) and state-contingent scale tilts expand investment; implemented jointly, they deliver super-additive gains.

title: Intermediation Dynamics in Corporate Bond Markets
affiliations: , University of Stuttgart and Karlsruhe Institute of Technology

detail.title: Intermediation Dynamics in Corporate Bond Markets
detail.abstract: This paper analyzes the dynamic interactions among four major U.S. corporate bond intermediary types-dealers, insurers, mutual funds, and ETFs. We document strong interdependencies among these intermediary types, with dealer inventories responding to the trading activity of mutual funds and ETFs. Insurance companies often adjust positions in the opposite direction of mutual funds and ETFs. Shocks to one intermediary can have long-lasting impacts on the other intermediaries. During bond downgrades, insurers sell to mutual funds, facilitated by dealers who provide liquidity to both sides of the trade.

title: Pulse of the Cryptomarkets: Revisiting Systematic and Idiosyncratic Risks through High-Frequency Connectedness
affiliations: Université de Rennes 1, University of Economics Ho Chi Minh City, Université de Rennes 1 and Univ Rennes, CNRS, CREM - UMR6211, F-35000 Rennes (France)

detail.title: Pulse of the Cryptomarkets: Revisiting Systematic and Idiosyncratic Risks through High-Frequency Connectedness
detail.abstract: This paper investigates the high-frequency connectedness of cryptocurrency markets and revisits the canonical distinction between systematic and idiosyncratic risk. We examine market-wide and cluster-level risk propagation for approximately fifty cryptocurrencies at a 30-minute frequency from 2021 to 2024. Their proximity and divergence patterns suggest a grouping into fifteen clusters. Connectedness in returns is analysed using both linear VAR models—capturing average behaviour—and quantile VAR models—to account for asymmetries—under a time–frequency decomposition. Given the large dataset, the tractability of the time variation is addressed through a rolling estimation. This framework enables the measurement of the speed, magnitude, and asymmetries of shock transmission, as well as its temporal dynamics. We find evidence of extremely high connectedness, with transmission occurring predominantly in the very short horizon: more than half of the spillover takes place within less than one hour. Net transmitters in the short horizon, such as Bitcoin, AAVE, and Uniswap, become net receivers over longer horizons as portfolio reallocations generate feedback effects. Strong asymmetries emerge from the quantile-based connectedness: negative shocks diffuse more slowly, reflecting a wait-and-see behaviour, whereas positive shocks propagate more rapidly under fear-of-missing-out dynamics. Overall, the traditional boundary between diversifiable and non-diversifiable risk appears porous. Our findings contribute to a deeper understanding of risk propagation, highlighting that local shocks at inception can quickly acquire systematic proportions.

title: The Impact of SEC v. Jarkesy on Civil Tax Fraud Penalties.
affiliations: Texas Tech University School of Law

detail.title: The Impact of SEC v. Jarkesy on Civil Tax Fraud Penalties.
detail.abstract:
This Article considers whether the recent Supreme Court case, SEC v. Jarkesy, 144 S. Ct. 2117 (2024) now requires jury trials for assertions of civil tax fraud penalties.  While no jury has ever been required in such cases since 1982, the Jarkesy opinion potentially changes the analysis. 

This article argues that the impact of Jarkesy depends on how one balances government needs against individual liberty interests when considering how and when the Constitution requires Article III court involvement in executive branch operations. Jarkesy inverts prior teachings on how courts should perform that balancing. Some will conclude that adjudicating tax fraud in the Tax Court does not violate the Seventh Amendment. However, the result in Jarkesy, the logic by which it reached that result, and recent changes in tax administration, together open a plausible path for others to disagree.

Part I provides a basic understanding of how the civil tax fraud penalty is administered and its history. The history contains some surprises. Part II explains the traditional justifications for why the Seventh Amendment would not apply to assertion of tax fraud penalties. Part III evaluates whether the new logic given in Jarkesy—read in light of the penalty’s history and in light of a revised understanding of tax administration—now supports a contrary conclusion.

title: Calendar Edge in the C-Suite: CEO Relative Age, Stress Management, and Firm Results
affiliations: University of Maryland, The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK) - CUHK Business School, The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK) - CUHK Business School, University of Virginia and Baylor University - Hankamer School of Business

detail.title: Calendar Edge in the C-Suite: CEO Relative Age, Stress Management, and Firm Results
detail.abstract: Using relative age (i.e., age at school entry relative to cohort due to state-level eligibility cutoffs) as a proxy for self-efficacy, we examine whether CEO self-efficacy is positively associated with firm performance, especially when CEOs face high-stress tasks.
